Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the FCIC-approved form inventory for the MPCI/crop book (Notice of Loss, Production Worksheet, Claim for Indemnity, Summary of Coverage); escalates contested form standards to Regulatory Counsel and the RMA Regional Office

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 7 CFR 457.8 Basic Provisions sec. 1 (definition of 'claim for indemnity') and sec. 14 re-read on eCFR, together with 2026 SRA Section IV(f)(1) and the RMA Document and Supplemental Standards Handbook (DSSH, FCIC-24040) for the reinsurance year, at every form release

In-scope processes.value: Crop form design and claim correspondence authoring for every FCIC-approved plan of insurance the AIP delivers — loss notice intake, appraisal/production worksheet, claim for indemnity, and the acreage/production report packet, by crop, plan code and state

In-scope systems.value: Crop policy admin form library and correspondence template set; signed PDF masters mastered in the document management repository and pushed to the agent portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: Crop Form Standards Procedure — DSSH layout conformance, section 14 mandatory-element matrix, ADM/Special Provisions dependency check, RMA Regional Office submission of AIP-created forms, edition versioning by reinsurance year

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Claims Director / Manager; re-approved each reinsurance year before the earliest sales closing date (Nov 30 fall crops / Mar 15 spring crops)

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the approved edition must be in production before the crop's sales closing date, and any policy or claim record it produces must clear the weekly RMA transaction cutoff date for the Data Acceptance System

Deadline reminders configured.value: Form release calendar alerts at 90/60/30 days before the earliest sales closing date for each affected crop, plus a standing weekly alert two days ahead of the DAS transaction cutoff

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory extract, DSSH conformance checklists, RMA approval correspondence and dated PDF masters retained for the crop year plus 3 years and made available to FCIC on request per SRA Section IV record-retention

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any indemnity accepted on a superseded or non-approved form is logged with policy number, crop, crop year, the missing section 14 element and the re-execution/correction date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every AIP-created form released without prior RMA written approval and every claim re-executed on a corrected form

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All crop forms and claim correspondence templates active in the reinsurance year, plus every claim for indemnity accepted in the crop year, keyed by policy number, crop code, plan code and state

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — an indemnity accepted on a form absent from the FCIC-approved inventory, or missing any section 14 mandatory element, is a fail; 2 or more fails renders form control ineffective and triggers an RMA self-disclosure assessment

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous/per change; conformance is tested at every form release and a full-inventory sweep runs once per reinsurance year before the earliest sales closing date

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have authored or approved any sampled form edition or correspondence template

Evidence location for test results.value: Form conformance workpaper (inventory extract, DSSH checklists, sampled executed claim forms, exception list) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C01/<reinsurance year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory with RMA approval references, DSSH checklists and sampled executed claim forms, producible to an RMA Regional Compliance Office or USDA OIG request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns correspondence with the RMA Regional Office and Risk Management Services Division; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that a non-approved form was used before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Pull the FCIC-approved document set for the reinsurance year
actions: Download from RMA's public Appendix III/Actuarial Information Browser the reinsurance-year Basic Provisions (7 CFR 457.8), the Crop Provisions for every crop the AIP writes, and the Special Provisions of Insurance by state and county.
Download the Actuarial Data Master (ADM) files for the reinsurance year and note the release date printed on the ADM download page.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager for the crop/plan/state matrix the AIP will actually sell so the form scope matches the book.
File the whole set in the document management repository under Crop/RY<year>/FCIC-source and lock it read-only as the baseline for this release.
checklist.done: the reinsurance-year Basic Provisions, Crop Provisions, Special Provisions and ADM release are filed as a locked, dated baseline covering every crop/state the AIP sells.

checklist.step: Diff this reinsurance year's FCIC documents against last year's
actions: Run a redline of the new Basic Provisions and each Crop Provisions against the prior crop year edition and list every changed section number.
Read the RMA Manager's Bulletins and Product Management Bulletins (PM-xx) issued since the last release and record any that change form content, wording or required statements.
Flag every change touching sec. 14 (Duties in the Event of Damage or Loss), sec. 1 definitions, notice deadlines or signature requirements as form-impacting.
Hand the impacted-section list to the Policy Forms Specialist with a due date set 30 days before the earliest sales closing date.
checklist.done: a dated change list names every FCIC document section and RMA bulletin that changes form content this reinsurance year, with owners and due dates.

checklist.step: Build the section 14 mandatory-element matrix for the claim for indemnity
actions: Open 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 14 and list each element the claim form must capture: date of damage, cause of loss, unit number and unit structure, acreage by practice/type, appraised and harvested production, records of production by unit, share, and the insured's signature and date.
Add the sec. 1 definition of 'claim for indemnity' to the matrix header so the form is scoped to a signed, complete submission and not a bare notice of loss.
Add the Loss Adjustment Standards Handbook (LASH/FCIC-25010) data requirements for the crop's loss method (appraisal worksheet, production worksheet, special case entries).
Map every matrix row to a printed field on the draft form and mark any row with no field as a gap.
Send the matrix to the Claims Director / Manager for confirmation that adjusters can actually complete each field in the field.
checklist.done: every sec. 14 element and LASH data requirement maps to a named printed field, with zero unmapped rows.

checklist.step: Draft the AIP-created forms to DSSH layout standards
actions: Open the Document and Supplemental Standards Handbook (DSSH, FCIC-24040) and apply the standards for form title, AIP name and address block, form identifier, edition/version date and page x of y numbering.
Reproduce FCIC-mandated wording verbatim where DSSH says 'must read as follows' — never paraphrase policy language into plain English.
Set the edition date in the footer to the reinsurance year (e.g. 'RY2026 rev 09/2025') so superseded editions are visually distinguishable in the field.
Confirm the form carries the crop, plan code and unit identifiers needed to key the record to the policy in the Data Acceptance System.
Save the draft as <formID>-RY<year>-draft.pdf in the release folder.
checklist.done: each AIP-created form carries a DSSH-conformant identifier, edition date and page numbering, with FCIC-mandated wording reproduced verbatim.

checklist.step: Add the federally mandated statements and warnings
actions: Add the current USDA nondiscrimination statement in full, using the wording published by USDA for the program year, with the program discrimination complaint filing instructions.
Add the Privacy Act statement covering the authority (Federal Crop Insurance Act, 7 U.S.C. 1501 et seq.), purpose, routine uses and the voluntary/mandatory nature of the disclosure.
Add the false-statement warning citing 18 U.S.C. 1006 and 1014 and 7 U.S.C. 1506(n), immediately above the insured's signature line on the claim for indemnity.
Add the OMB control number and Paperwork Reduction Act burden statement where the form collects information on FCIC's behalf.
Initial and date the legal review sheet and return the annotated PDF to the Policy Forms Specialist.
checklist.done: nondiscrimination, Privacy Act, false-statement and PRA statements appear in full on every affected form, with a dated counsel review sheet.

checklist.step: Reconcile the draft forms to the ADM and Special Provisions data
actions: Check every coded field on the form (crop code, type, practice, unit structure, coverage level, price election) against the ADM code tables for the reinsurance year.
Check the Special Provisions for state/county-specific reporting requirements that need a printed field or footnote (e.g. organic certification, added land, written agreements).
Where a Special Provision demands a statement on the form, add it and reference the SP document number on the drafting sheet.
Log the ADM release date used, because a later ADM release re-opens this reconciliation.
checklist.done: every coded field validates against the reinsurance-year ADM tables and each state Special Provision requirement is either printed on the form or documented as not applicable.

checklist.step: Route the draft package for internal review and sign-off
actions: Open a form-release case and attach the drafts, the sec. 14 matrix, the counsel review sheet and the ADM reconciliation.
Route in parallel to the Claims Director / Manager (field usability and LASH alignment), Regulatory Counsel (mandated wording) and the Policy Admin Ops Lead (system printability).
Set a 10 business day review SLA and record each reviewer's decision — approve, approve with edits, reject — on the case.
Re-circulate any form that changed after a reviewer approved it; do not carry forward stale approvals.
checklist.done: each form in the release carries three dated internal approvals against the exact version being published.

checklist.step: Submit AIP-created forms to RMA for approval
actions: Prepare the RMA submission package per DSSH: cover letter naming the AIP and reinsurance year, the form PDF, a redline against the previously approved edition, and a statement of the FCIC procedure the form implements.
Send the package to the assigned RMA Regional Office / Product Administration and Standards Division mailbox and log the submission date and RMA reference in the Internal Regulatory System.
Track the response; on an RMA objection, record the objection text, the corrective edit and the resubmission date on the same record.
Do not release a form to production until the RMA written approval or the DSSH self-certification basis is recorded on the submission record.
checklist.done: every AIP-created form has a logged RMA submission with either a written approval or a documented DSSH self-certification basis before release.

checklist.step: Version, publish and lock the approved masters
actions: Publish the approved PDF master under Crop/RY<year>/approved-forms with the form ID and edition date in the filename.
Set metadata: form ID, edition date, crops covered, states covered, RMA approval reference, effective sales closing date, superseded edition ID.
Mark the prior edition 'Superseded — do not use after <sales closing date>' and move it to the archive view.
Confirm the repository search returns the new edition by form ID, crop and state.
checklist.done: the approved master is published with full metadata and the prior edition is marked superseded with an end-use date.

checklist.step: Load the approved forms into the policy and claims form libraries
actions: Load each approved PDF/template into the crop form library with an effective-date range starting no later than the earliest sales closing date.
Bind the claim for indemnity template to the claim transaction type in the claims platform so no other template can be selected for a crop indemnity.
Set the prior edition to expire the day before the new effective date so it cannot be selected for a new crop year record.
Hand the configuration ticket to the QA Analyst with the form IDs and effective dates to be tested.
checklist.done: the new editions are effective-dated in the form library and the superseded editions are no longer selectable for the new crop year.

checklist.step: Test-print and test-execute the forms before release
actions: In the pre-production environment generate a claim for indemnity for one policy per crop and per unit structure (basic, optional, enterprise, whole-farm).
Check that every sec. 14 field prints populated or blank-but-present, that the signature block and false-statement warning are on the same page, and that no field is truncated.
Generate the same form at the largest expected acreage/unit count to confirm continuation pages number correctly.
Log defects to the release ticket and re-test after fix; do not accept a 'cosmetic' classification on a missing mandated statement.
checklist.done: test-generated forms across every unit structure print all sec. 14 fields and mandated statements with no truncation, and all defects are closed.

checklist.step: Brief agents and loss adjusters on the changed forms
actions: Publish a form-change bulletin listing form ID, edition date, what changed, the first crop year it applies to and the date the old edition stops being accepted.
Post a short module to the LMS covering the new/changed sec. 14 fields and assign it to every appointed crop agent and loss adjuster.
Tell the Agency Relations Manager to push the bulletin through the agent portal and to confirm receipt from each agency principal.
Track completion and chase non-completers weekly until the sales closing date.
checklist.done: the bulletin is issued and every active crop agent and loss adjuster has an LMS completion record before the sales closing date.

checklist.step: Block acceptance of superseded editions at intake
actions: Add an intake validation that reads the form ID and edition date on the received claim and rejects any edition outside the effective range for the crop year.
Instruct the Claims Intake Rep to return a superseded form to the adjuster for re-execution rather than keying it and correcting later.
Create a daily exception queue for rejected submissions so re-executions are chased inside 3 business days.
Report the weekly rejection count to the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: intake rejects superseded editions automatically and rejected claims are re-executed on the current edition within 3 business days.

checklist.step: Update the form inventory register
actions: Add one register row per form: form ID, edition date, crops, states, FCIC/RMA approval reference, sec. 14 matrix version, effective date, superseded edition, owner.
Reconcile the register row count to the form library extract from the policy admin platform and resolve any difference the same day.
Mark the register 'complete for RY<year>' and have the Compliance Manager countersign it.
checklist.done: the register reconciles line-for-line to the live form library and is countersigned for the reinsurance year.

checklist.step: Retain the release evidence for the SRA retention period
actions: Move the release folder (drafts, sec. 14 matrix, counsel review sheet, RMA submission and approval, QA test output, bulletin, register) into the evidence repository under REG-056/C01/RY<year>.
Apply the crop-year-plus-3-years retention label required for records made available to FCIC under the SRA.
Confirm the record is retrievable by form ID, crop code and reinsurance year.
checklist.done: the full release evidence package is filed with a crop-year-plus-3 retention label and is retrievable by form ID and crop year.

testing.step: Build the population of forms in use and claims accepted
actions: Extract every claim for indemnity with a signed date inside the crop year, with policy number, crop code, plan code, state, unit structure, form ID and form edition date.
Extract the live crop form library from the policy administration platform with effective-date ranges.
Reconcile the distinct form IDs appearing on claims to the form library extract and list any form ID on a claim that is not in the library.
testing.done: the claim population and the form library extract are reconciled and any unlisted form ID is carried forward as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the form inventory register to the FCIC-approved source
actions: Compare each register row to the RMA approval correspondence or the recorded DSSH self-certification basis held in the Internal Regulatory System.
Confirm every AIP-created form in use has a submission record dated before its effective date.
List register rows with no approval reference, and library forms with no register row, as separate exception classes.
testing.done: every form in use traces to a dated RMA submission record, or is listed as an unapproved-form exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of forms newly introduced or amended this reinsurance year.
Take 30 executed claims for indemnity by seeded random selection, stratified to cover each crop with more than 50 claims and each unit structure.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all new/amended forms and is stratified across crops and unit structures.

testing.step: Re-perform the section 14 completeness check independently
actions: Read 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 14 directly and build your own element list before looking at the AIP's matrix.
Open each sampled executed claim in the claim file repository and tick each element against the printed and completed fields.
Treat a present-but-blank mandatory field on a signed claim as a fail, not a documentation gap.
Compare your element list to the AIP's matrix and log any element the matrix omits.
testing.done: each sampled claim has an independent element-by-element assessment and any omission in the AIP's own matrix is documented.

testing.step: Verify the mandated federal statements are present and current
actions: Compare the nondiscrimination statement on each sampled form to the USDA wording published for that program year, word for word.
Confirm the false-statement warning cites 18 U.S.C. 1006/1014 and 7 U.S.C. 1506(n) and sits immediately above the signature line.
Confirm the Privacy Act statement names the Federal Crop Insurance Act authority and the routine uses.
Log any paraphrased or prior-year wording as a fail with the exact deviation quoted.
testing.done: every sampled form carries current, verbatim nondiscrimination, false-statement and Privacy Act wording, or the deviation is quoted in the workpaper.

testing.step: Trace each sampled claim to its policy and unit identifiers
actions: Match the policy number, crop code, plan code, county and unit number on the claim form to the policy record for the same crop year.
Confirm the insured's share on the form matches the share on the acreage report of record.
Confirm the signed claim date is on or after the date of damage recorded on the notice of loss.
Flag any identifier mismatch, because a mismatch will also break the Type 21 claim record sent to RMA.
testing.done: every sampled claim's identifiers and share reconcile to the policy and acreage record, or the mismatch is listed.

testing.step: Recompute the edition-effectivity and cutoff timing
actions: For each sampled claim, compare the form edition date on the executed document to the edition effective for that crop's sales closing date.
Confirm the resulting claim record was transmitted no later than the weekly transaction cutoff date following claim acceptance.
Recompute, for 10 sampled claims, the days between signature date and transmission and list any exceeding the cutoff window.
Any claim accepted on an edition superseded before that crop's sales closing date is a breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled claim was accepted on a superseded edition and every sampled claim record cleared its weekly transaction cutoff.

testing.step: Test that superseded editions are genuinely blocked
actions: Attempt, in the pre-production environment, to key a crop indemnity against a superseded form ID and record the system response.
Attempt to select a form outside its effective-date range for the crop year and record the response.
Capture screenshots of both attempts into the workpaper as control-operation evidence.
Report any successful bypass to the Compliance Manager the same day.
testing.done: both bypass attempts are rejected by the system, with screenshots filed, or the bypass is escalated same day.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with policy number, crop, crop year, form ID/edition and the specific sec. 14 element or mandated statement missing.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: stale edition in the field, library effective-dating error, wording not refreshed, adjuster completion gap, intake control bypass.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and open a re-execution task for any claim paid on a deficient form.
Refer any pattern suggesting an unapproved form was used at scale to Regulatory Counsel for an RMA self-disclosure assessment.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a coded root cause, an owner, a remediation date and — where a claim was paid — a re-execution task.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate over the sample and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for missing sec. 14 elements.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with a reference to each supporting workpaper section.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled form edition, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any RMA self-disclosure recommendation to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under REG-056/C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns generation and delivery of every crop policyholder notice — Summary of Coverage, acreage/production report packets, premium billing, termination for indebtedness and claim determination letters — against the RMA date calendar

In-scope systems.value: Crop policy admin correspondence engine and print/mail queue, with delivery status written back to the notice log and mirrored to the agent portal

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Indemnity paid within 30 days of the signed claim for indemnity; suspected fraud/misrepresentation referred to RMA within 3 business days of discovery; Plan of Operations items due by April 1; FCIC responses due within 45 days; every resulting record transmitted by the weekly transaction cutoff

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven with an annual April 1 anchor; the timeliness test runs quarterly on the quarter's notice population and in full ahead of the annual Plan of Operations submission

checklist.step: Rebuild the reinsurance-year crop date calendar
actions: Pull, per crop, state and county, the sales closing date, cancellation date, termination date, acreage reporting date, production reporting date, premium billing date and end of insurance period from the reinsurance-year Special Provisions and the Basic Provisions.
Add the fixed federal anchors: April 1 Plan of Operations submission, the weekly transaction cutoff date, the 30-day indemnity payment clock and the 3-business-day fraud referral clock.
Load each date as a dated row keyed on crop/state/county and stamp the source document number on the row.
Send the loaded calendar to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Claims Director / Manager for confirmation before it drives any notice.
checklist.done: every crop/state/county date row is loaded with its source document reference and confirmed by policy administration and claims.

checklist.step: Define each notice type, its trigger and its statutory day count
actions: Build one row per notice: Summary of Coverage, revised Summary of Coverage after an acreage revision, premium billing statement, notice of debt/termination for indebtedness, cancellation notice, notice of loss acknowledgement, claim payment advice and claim denial letter.
Set the trigger event and its system source field for each — acreage report acceptance date, billing date, signed claim date, denial determination date.
Set the day count and its basis (calendar vs business days) and record the citation: 30 days from the signed claim for indemnity for payment, 3 business days for a fraud referral.
Name the delivery channel and the proof-of-delivery artifact for each row (mail with USPS proof, eDelivery with timestamp and open status, agent portal posting).
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm every day count and basis in writing.
checklist.done: each notice type has a trigger field, a cited day count, a delivery channel and a named proof-of-delivery artifact, confirmed by counsel.

checklist.step: Wire the triggers into the correspondence engine
actions: Configure each notice trigger to fire off the system event, not a manual queue — acreage report acceptance, billing run completion, claim approval posting, denial determination posting.
Set the generation SLA inside the statutory window (e.g. generate the claim payment advice within 5 days of approval so the 30-day payment clock is never the binding constraint).
Write the trigger date, generation date and channel back to the notice log for every notice produced.
Raise a ticket with the Configuration Engineer for any notice still produced by manual request and schedule its automation.
checklist.done: every in-scope notice is event-triggered with generation and trigger dates written to the notice log, and manual-only notices have automation tickets.

checklist.step: Validate the address of record before every mailing run
actions: Run the address-of-record extract against the CASS/NCOA validation service and quarantine undeliverable addresses before the run, not after.
For quarantined policies, ask the servicing agent through the agent portal to confirm the current mailing address within 3 business days.
Record the confirmed address and its source on the policy so the notice log shows what address the notice actually went to.
Never suppress a statutory notice for a bad address — deliver to the last known address and log the attempt.
checklist.done: the mailing run uses validated addresses, quarantined cases have an agent-confirmed address or a logged delivery attempt, and no statutory notice is suppressed.

checklist.step: Generate and release the Summary of Coverage after acreage reporting
actions: After the acreage reporting date, process accepted acreage reports and generate the Summary of Coverage showing units, acres, share, practice/type, coverage level, price election and liability by unit.
Check the liability and premium figures on the Summary against the rating output for the same crop year before release.
Release the run to print/eDelivery and record the release date and channel per policy in the notice log.
Regenerate and reissue a revised Summary whenever an acreage revision is accepted, and log it as a separate notice event.
checklist.done: every policy with an accepted acreage report has a released Summary of Coverage with unit-level liability, and every revision has a reissued Summary logged separately.

checklist.step: Issue premium billing and the debt/termination sequence on the federal dates
actions: Generate the premium billing statement ahead of the premium billing date for the crop, showing gross premium, subsidy, producer premium, administrative fees and the date interest attaches.
Run the delinquency extract after the premium due date and generate the notice of debt showing the amount owed and the termination date if unpaid.
Generate the termination for indebtedness notice on the termination date for the crop and record it as a statutory notice in the notice log.
Give the ineligibility list to the Compliance Analyst for the RMA ineligible-tracking submission so terminated producers are not re-written.
checklist.done: billing, debt and termination notices are issued on the federal dates for each crop with the ineligibility list handed to compliance.

checklist.step: Acknowledge notices of loss and start the claim clocks
actions: On receipt of a notice of loss, record the date and time of receipt, the date of damage and the cause of loss, and issue the acknowledgement to the insured and the servicing agent.
Assign the loss adjuster and start the inspection clock, recording the assignment date on the claim.
Start the 30-day indemnity payment clock at the date the insured signs the claim for indemnity — not at first notice — and display both dates on the claim header.
Escalate to the Claims Director / Manager any claim where the adjuster cannot inspect before the crop is destroyed or harvested.
checklist.done: every notice of loss has a dated acknowledgement, an assigned adjuster, and a claim header showing both the loss date and the signed-claim date driving the 30-day clock.

checklist.step: Pay or deny the claim inside the 30-day window and notify in writing
actions: Work the claim queue in signed-claim-date order and monitor the days-to-30 counter on each open claim daily.
On approval, release payment and generate the payment advice showing the indemnity calculation by unit — production to count, guarantee, price election and share.

On denial, generate the denial letter stating the specific policy provision relied on, the factual basis, and the insured's rights to mediation, arbitration under 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 20, and appeal to the USDA National Appeals Division.
Log the generation and delivery dates of the payment advice or denial letter in the notice log against the claim.
Escalate any claim reaching day 25 without a determination to the Claims Director / Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every claim is paid or denied with a written notice inside 30 days of the signed claim, with the calculation or the cited denial basis stated in the notice.

checklist.step: Refer suspected fraud, waste or abuse to RMA within 3 business days
actions: On any indication of misrepresentation, false production records or unreported acreage, open an SIU case and stamp the discovery date and time.
Prepare the referral with policy number, crop year, crop, the specific facts, the documents relied on and the AIP's action to date.
Send the referral to the RMA Regional Compliance Office within 3 business days of discovery and record the sent date and the RMA acknowledgement reference on the case.
Notify Regulatory Counsel and hold any claim payment pending the referral outcome where the policy allows it.
Review the open referral queue daily so no case ages past the 3-business-day clock.
checklist.done: every suspected fraud case has a dated RMA referral sent within 3 business days of discovery with the RMA acknowledgement recorded.

checklist.step: Answer FCIC and RMA correspondence inside the 45-day window
actions: Log every FCIC/RMA letter, finding or data-mining referral on receipt with the received date and the computed 45-day due date.
Assign an owner and a draft-due date at day 25 so review and counsel clearance fit inside the window.
Attach the response, the supporting records and the transmission confirmation to the same record on send.
Where more time is genuinely needed, request an extension in writing before the due date and record RMA's answer — never let the date pass silently.
checklist.done: every FCIC/RMA item has a computed 45-day due date and a sent response or a written, granted extension before that date.

checklist.step: Prepare the April 1 annual submission items
actions: Work back from April 1 and set internal due dates for each component of the Plan of Operations submission and any annual notice or certification RMA requires with it.
Collect the components from the Controller (financial data), the Claims Director / Manager (adjuster and QC data) and the Corporate Secretary (governance certifications).
Assemble, review and submit the package to RMA by April 1 and record the submission confirmation on the regulatory record.
Log any RMA request for revision and track it under the same 45-day response discipline.
checklist.done: the annual submission is complete and transmitted to RMA by April 1 with a stored confirmation and any revision requests tracked.

checklist.step: Transmit resulting records by the weekly transaction cutoff
actions: Queue the policy, acreage and claim records generated by the week's notices for the RMA Data Acceptance System transmission.
Run the pre-submission edit check and clear rejects before the cutoff, escalating unfixable rejects to the Data Quality Analyst the same day.
Transmit no later than the transaction cutoff date for the week and store the acceptance report against the batch.
Reconcile accepted record counts to the notice log counts for the week and investigate any gap.
checklist.done: the week's records are transmitted before the cutoff with a stored acceptance report reconciling to the notice log counts.

checklist.step: Work the returned-mail and failed-delivery queue
actions: Scan returned mail and failed eDelivery bounces into the policy record within 2 business days of receipt.
For statutory notices, re-issue to a corrected address obtained from the servicing agent and log the second attempt with its date.
Escalate to the Policy Admin Ops Lead any termination or claim denial notice that failed delivery, because the policyholder's rights turn on it.
Close each returned-mail item with a disposition code: redelivered, address corrected, undeliverable-agent notified.
checklist.done: every returned or bounced notice is logged, statutory notices are re-issued, and each item is closed with a disposition code.

checklist.step: Run the weekly notice-timeliness monitor
actions: Publish a weekly view of days from trigger to delivery by notice type, with the statutory day count as a reference line.
Flag every open claim over 20 days from signed-claim date and every fraud referral over 2 business days old.
Send the exception list to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and the Claims Director / Manager each Monday with named owners.
Escalate any breach of a statutory day count to the Compliance Officer within one business day.
checklist.done: a weekly timeliness view is published, aged items are assigned to named owners, and every statutory breach is escalated within one business day.

checklist.step: Retain the notice evidence for the SRA retention period
actions: Archive the notice log extract, PDF renders, proof-of-delivery records and returned-mail dispositions per crop year.
Apply the crop-year-plus-3-years retention label required for records available to FCIC under the SRA.
Confirm retrieval by policy number, crop year and notice type returns the notice PDF and its delivery record together.
checklist.done: notice evidence is archived with a crop-year-plus-3 label and retrievable by policy number, crop year and notice type.

testing.step: Build the notice population for the period
actions: Extract every notice with a trigger event in the quarter: policy number, crop year, notice type, trigger date, generation date, delivery date, channel and delivery status.
Extract in parallel the underlying events — accepted acreage reports, billing runs, signed claims for indemnity, denial determinations, SIU discovery dates.
Reconcile event count to notice count by type and list every event with no corresponding notice as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the notice population reconciles to the underlying event counts and every noticeless event is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Tie the signed-claim count to the claims platform claim register for the same period and the billing notice count to the billing run control totals.
Tie the fraud referral count to the SIU case register discovery dates.
Resolve every difference with the Policy Admin Ops Lead before drawing the sample, and note the reconciliation in the workpaper.
testing.done: notice counts agree with the claims register, billing control totals and SIU case register, with differences resolved and documented.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of claim payment advices, claim denial letters, termination for indebtedness notices and RMA fraud referrals.
Take 25 servicing notices (Summary of Coverage, revised Summary, billing) by seeded random selection across crops and states.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of statutory notices and a reproducible random selection of servicing notices.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day indemnity clock
actions: For each sampled paid claim, read the insured's signature date on the executed claim for indemnity in the claim file — not the system-entered date — and the payment issue date.
Recompute elapsed calendar days and compare to 30.
Where a claim exceeded 30 days, confirm whether interest was calculated and paid, and quantify it.
Confirm the payment advice was generated and delivered, not just the payment released.
testing.done: every sampled paid claim has a recomputed day count from the signed claim date, with late cases quantified and interest treatment verified.

testing.step: Recompute the 3-business-day fraud referral clock
actions: For each sampled SIU case, read the discovery date and time from the case narrative and the referral sent date from the RMA correspondence record.
Recompute business days excluding federal holidays and compare to 3.
Confirm the RMA acknowledgement reference is stored and that the referral names the policy, crop year and the specific facts.
Treat a referral with no acknowledgement reference as unproven delivery, not merely undocumented.
testing.done: every sampled referral has a recomputed business-day count from documented discovery and a stored RMA acknowledgement.

testing.step: Re-perform the content check on statutory notices
actions: Read each sampled denial letter and confirm it names the specific policy provision, the factual basis, and the mediation, arbitration (7 CFR 457.8 sec. 20) and National Appeals Division rights.
Read each sampled termination notice and confirm it states the amount owed, the termination date and the reinstatement conditions.
Read each sampled Summary of Coverage and confirm unit-level liability, share, coverage level and price election are shown.
Log any notice missing a required element with the missing element quoted.
testing.done: every sampled statutory notice carries its required content elements, or the missing element is quoted in the workpaper.

testing.step: Trace delivery to proof, not just to generation
actions: For each sampled notice, open the archived PDF render and confirm it matches the notice type and the policy identifiers.
Confirm a proof-of-delivery artifact exists: mail manifest entry, eDelivery timestamp, or logged second attempt for returned mail.
Compare the mailing address on the render to the validated address of record at the trigger date.
Flag any notice with a generation record but no delivery artifact.
testing.done: every sampled notice has an archived render, a matching address of record and a proof-of-delivery artifact, or is flagged.

testing.step: Test the April 1 and 45-day federal date compliance
actions: Confirm the annual submission transmission confirmation is dated on or before April 1 and covers every required component.
List every FCIC/RMA item received in the period, recompute its 45-day due date from the received date and compare to the response sent date.
Confirm any extension was requested in writing before the due date and granted in writing.
Confirm the week's record batches were transmitted on or before each weekly transaction cutoff date, using the stored acceptance reports.
testing.done: the April 1 submission, every 45-day response and every weekly cutoff transmission are evidenced as on time or documented as late.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with policy number, crop year, notice type, days late and the policyholder impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: trigger not fired, manual queue backlog, address quarantine, claim queue aging, adjuster delay, referral not opened at discovery.
Assign an owner and remediation date; for late indemnities open an interest-calculation task, and for late referrals notify Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment, with interest and counsel tasks opened where required.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute timeliness rates by notice type and compare to the 100% statutory / 98% servicing thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the day-count recomputation sections.
Have the independent reviewer, who generated no sampled notice, sign and date the workpaper.
Report late statutory notices and late RMA referrals to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C02.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with timeliness rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Take in the reinsurance-year configuration requirements
actions: Open a reinsurance-year configuration epic and pull in the date calendar rows, form editions and mandated content elements from the Compliance Analyst and the Policy Forms Specialist.
Add the RMA M13 record-layout changes for Type 10 (policy), Type 11 (acreage), Type 13/14 (production), Type 15 (yield) and Type 21 (claim) records for the reinsurance year.
Write one story per enforceable rule with the citation (e.g. 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 14 element, SRA Section IV(d) date) in the story description.
Set the epic's hard date to 30 days before the earliest sales closing date so there is soak time.
checklist.done: every enforceable FCIC date, form and content rule exists as a cited story under a dated reinsurance-year epic.

checklist.step: Load and reconcile the Actuarial Data Master tables
actions: Download the reinsurance-year ADM files from RMA and load the crop, type, practice, unit structure, coverage level, price and rate tables into the staging schema.
Row-count and checksum each loaded table against the RMA file manifest and record both in the load log.
Diff the new tables against the prior reinsurance year and publish the changed-code list to the Business Systems Analyst and the Pricing Actuary.
Promote to production only when the variance report shows zero unexplained rows, and re-run the whole load on any ADM re-release.
checklist.done: ADM tables are loaded with zero unexplained variance against the RMA manifest and the changed-code list is published.

checklist.step: Configure the hard-stop date edits
actions: Set a hard stop preventing a new application or coverage change from being accepted after the crop/state sales closing date.

Set a hard stop preventing acceptance of an acreage report after the acreage reporting date, and of production reports after the production reporting date, without a documented written agreement reference.
Set the cancellation and termination dates to drive automatic status changes rather than manual intervention.
Classify each edit hard-stop vs warning in the configuration register and record who approved any warning-only classification.
Deploy through a change record naming the citation the edit enforces.
checklist.done: each federal date is enforced by a classified, change-controlled edit with an approver recorded for every warning-only classification.

checklist.step: Configure form effective-dating and selection control
actions: Set the effective-date range on every crop form edition so a superseded edition cannot be selected for a new crop year record.
Bind the claim for indemnity template exclusively to the crop indemnity transaction so no generic template can be substituted.
Make the sec. 14 fields mandatory at save — date of damage, cause of loss, unit number, acres, share, production to count, insured signature date.
Confirm with the Policy Forms Specialist that the loaded edition IDs match the approved form inventory register exactly.
checklist.done: form editions are effective-dated, the indemnity template is bound to the transaction, sec. 14 fields are mandatory, and edition IDs reconcile to the register.

checklist.step: Configure the indemnity calculation to the FCIC procedure
actions: Configure the indemnity formula per crop and plan to the Loss Adjustment Standards Handbook method: guarantee by unit, production to count, price election, share and any prevented planting or replant factor.
Load the appraisal and quality adjustment factor tables from the reinsurance-year ADM rather than hand-keyed values.
Have the Pricing Actuary independently recompute five worked examples per crop and confirm the system output matches to the cent.
Lock the calculation configuration and require a change record for any adjustment mid-crop-year.
checklist.done: the indemnity calculation reproduces the actuary's worked examples to the cent for every crop and is locked under change control.

checklist.step: Build and validate the RMA record layouts
actions: Map each RMA record type to its source fields in the policy and claims systems and document the mapping field by field.
Implement the M13 field formats, lengths and code domains for the reinsurance year, sourcing all coded values from the loaded ADM tables.
Run the RMA pre-submission edit checks against a full simulated batch and drive the reject count to zero before release.
Store the mapping document and the dry-run edit report with the release record.
checklist.done: record builds pass the RMA edit checks on a full simulated batch with zero rejects, and the field mapping is documented and stored.

checklist.step: Configure the transaction cutoff scheduling
actions: Schedule the record build and transmission job to complete a full business day before the weekly transaction cutoff date, leaving room for reject rework.
Configure an alert to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst if the job has not completed or has open rejects 24 hours before cutoff.
Configure the acceptance report to be captured automatically and attached to the batch record.
Add a monitor comparing records eligible for transmission against records actually transmitted each week.
checklist.done: the transmission job runs a day ahead of cutoff with alerting, automatic acceptance-report capture and an eligible-versus-transmitted monitor.

checklist.step: Write the regression pack for the FCIC rules
actions: Write one regression case per enforced rule: after-sales-closing application rejected, late acreage report rejected, superseded form blocked, sec. 14 field mandatory, indemnity formula result.
Add negative cases attempting to bypass each hard stop and assert the exact system message returned.
Add a record-build case asserting field position and format for one record of each RMA type.
Link every case back to its cited story so coverage is traceable to the regulation.
checklist.done: every cited rule has a positive and a negative regression case linked back to its citation.

checklist.step: Execute the regression pack in pre-production
actions: Run the full pack against the release candidate with the reinsurance-year ADM loaded.
Attach evidence per case: the input record, the screen or API response, and the produced RMA record extract.
Fail the release on any bypassed hard stop or any indemnity variance, however small — a rounding difference on a federal indemnity is not cosmetic.
Publish the pass/fail summary to the Release Coordinator and the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the full regression pack executes with evidence per case and no bypassed hard stop or indemnity variance is carried into release.

checklist.step: Gate the release on compliance approval
actions: Attach the regression summary, ADM reconciliation and RMA dry-run edit report to the change record.
Require approval from the Head of IT, the Compliance Manager and the Policy Admin Ops Lead before deployment.
Schedule the deployment so it lands at least 14 days before the earliest sales closing date affected.
Record the back-out plan and the specific conditions that would trigger it.
checklist.done: the change record carries three named approvals, the evidence set and a dated back-out plan before deployment.

checklist.step: Verify the configuration in production after deployment
actions: Run the post-deployment smoke set: attempt one after-deadline application, one late acreage report and one superseded-form selection in production using a controlled test policy.
Export the live date-edit and form-effectivity configuration and diff it against the approved configuration register.
Confirm the ADM code tables in production match the promoted version by checksum.
Capture the smoke evidence and the diff into the release record within 24 hours of deployment.
checklist.done: production smoke tests reject all three attempts, the configuration diff is clean and the ADM checksum matches, all evidenced within 24 hours.

checklist.step: Control emergency changes and edit overrides
actions: Require an emergency change record for any configuration change made after a sales closing date, naming the crops and states exposed.
Require the Compliance Manager's written approval before any hard-stop edit is downgraded to a warning, with a fixed reversion date.
List the policies processed while the edit was relaxed and hand the list to the Compliance Analyst for review.
Confirm the reversion actually happened on the stated date and close the record with evidence.
checklist.done: every emergency change and edit downgrade has a compliance approval, an exposed-policy list, a reversion date and evidenced reversion.

checklist.step: Monitor RMA rejects and feed them back into configuration
actions: Publish a weekly view of RMA acceptance and reject counts by record type and reject reason code.
Group repeat reject codes and raise a configuration defect for any code appearing in three consecutive weeks.
Track each defect to a change record and confirm the reject code disappears in the following week's report.
Escalate any week where rejects exceed 2% of submitted records to the Head of IT and the Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: reject codes are trended weekly, repeat codes have configuration defects raised and closed, and any week above 2% is escalated.

checklist.step: Maintain the configuration register as the control inventory
actions: Keep one register row per enforced rule: rule description, citation, system, configuration object, hard stop vs warning, effective date, change record, owner.
Reconcile the register to a live configuration export at each release and after every emergency change.
Have the Compliance Manager countersign the register before the earliest sales closing date each reinsurance year.
checklist.done: the register reconciles to the live configuration export and is countersigned before the earliest sales closing date.

checklist.step: Retain the release evidence for the SRA retention period
actions: Archive change records, configuration exports, ADM load reconciliations, regression evidence and RMA acceptance reports by reinsurance year.
Apply the crop-year-plus-3-years retention label required for records available to FCIC.
Confirm retrieval by reinsurance year, rule citation and change record number returns the complete evidence set.
checklist.done: configuration evidence is archived with a crop-year-plus-3 label and retrievable by reinsurance year, citation and change record.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration changes and records produced
actions: Extract every change record touching crop policy, claims or RMA record-build configuration in the reinsurance year, with deployment date and approvers.
Extract the RMA transmission batches for the same period with record counts by type and acceptance status.
Reconcile the change extract to the deployment logs from the release pipeline and resolve any deployment with no change record before sampling.
testing.done: the change population reconciles to deployment logs with no unrecorded deployments outstanding.

testing.step: Reconcile the configuration register to the live system
actions: Export the live date edits, form effective-date ranges and mandatory-field settings from production.
Compare row by row to the configuration register and list register rows with no live counterpart and live settings with no register row.
Confirm every enforced rule in the register carries a citation, and challenge any rule with a generic reference.
testing.done: the live configuration export and the register reconcile row for row, with every rule carrying a specific citation.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of changes deployed within 30 days of a sales closing date and 100% of emergency changes and edit downgrades.
Take 20 further changes by seeded random selection across the reinsurance year.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all late and emergency changes plus a reproducible random selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the ADM reconciliation independently
actions: Download the reinsurance-year ADM files directly from RMA rather than using the AIP's staged copy.
Row-count and checksum the crop, practice, type, coverage level and price tables against production.
Sample 20 rate/price rows and compare values field by field to the RMA file.
Any variance is a fail — a wrong ADM value propagates into liability, premium and indemnity.
testing.done: production ADM tables match an independently downloaded RMA release on counts, checksums and 20 sampled rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the date-edit enforcement in the live system
actions: Using a controlled test policy in production, attempt to accept an application dated after the crop's sales closing date and record the exact system response.
Attempt to accept an acreage report after the acreage reporting date and a production report after the production reporting date.
Attempt to select a superseded form edition for a current crop year record.
Screenshot each rejection message into the workpaper; any acceptance is a control failure reported the same day.
testing.done: all three live bypass attempts are rejected with captured messages, or the acceptance is reported the same day as a control failure.

testing.step: Re-perform the indemnity calculation on real claims
actions: Select 10 paid claims across crops and unit structures and pull guarantee, production to count, price election and share from the claim file.
Recompute the indemnity by hand using the Loss Adjustment Standards Handbook method for that crop and plan.
Compare to the system-calculated indemnity to the cent and investigate any difference to its configuration source.
Confirm quality adjustment and prevented planting factors used came from the ADM tables, not manual entry.
testing.done: all 10 recomputed indemnities agree to the cent with factors traced to ADM sources, or the difference is traced to a named configuration defect.

testing.step: Trace produced records to RMA acceptance
actions: For each sampled batch, compare eligible record counts by type to submitted counts and to the RMA acceptance report.
List records eligible but never submitted and follow each to a resolution.
Open five accepted records per type and compare field values to the source policy or claim record.
Confirm the reject rework was resubmitted rather than abandoned.
testing.done: eligible, submitted and accepted counts reconcile, sampled record fields match source, and all rejects are evidenced as resubmitted.

testing.step: Recompute the cutoff and ADM-load timing
actions: For each week in the period, compare the transmission timestamp to the weekly transaction cutoff date and list every late batch.
Compare each ADM re-release publication date to the production load date and confirm the load fell inside 45 days.
Compare each configuration deployment date to the earliest affected sales closing date and list anything deployed after it.
Quantify the policies processed under an unenforced rule for every late deployment.
testing.done: every cutoff, ADM load and deployment date is recomputed against its deadline, with exposed policy counts quantified for late items.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the rule, the citation, the change record and the policies exposed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: rule not configured, edit downgraded, ADM load variance, mapping defect, deployment after deadline, reject rework abandoned.
Assign an owner and remediation date and require a regression case to be added for every configuration defect found.
Refer any case where records were never transmitted to Regulatory Counsel for an RMA disclosure assessment.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and a new regression case, with untransmitted-record cases referred to counsel.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the reject rate and the control-failure count and compare them to the 2% and zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the re-performance evidence.
Have the independent reviewer, who deployed no sampled change, sign and date the workpaper.
Report control failures and untransmitted records to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C03.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with reject rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.
