checklist.step: Extract the reinsurance-year training requirements into a matrix
actions: Read 2026 SRA Appendix IV and list each requirement as a matrix row: new loss adjusters need at least 60 hours of structured training including at least 24 classroom hours, a passed basic competency test before adjusting claims, annual refresher training, and records maintained subject to FCIC review.
Read RMA Manual 14 and add the agent-side rows: training on program dates, acreage/production reporting duties and eligibility rules before the sales season.
Read the Manager's Bulletins issued since last year and add any changed hour counts, topics or testing requirements with the bulletin number on the row.
Send the matrix to the Claims Director / Manager and Regulatory Counsel for written confirmation before curricula are built against it.
checklist.done: a confirmed requirements matrix lists every Appendix IV and Manual 14 training obligation with its citation and this year's changes flagged.

checklist.step: Build the roster of everyone who must be trained
actions: Extract employed loss adjusters from the HRIS with hire date, adjuster code and assigned states/crops.
Request the vendor adjuster roster from each loss-adjustment contractor with the same fields, and reject rosters missing adjuster codes.
Pull the appointed crop agent list from the agency/producer management system with agency, states and appointment dates.
Classify every person NEW (no prior reinsurance-year accreditation) or RETURNING, because the 60/24-hour requirement binds only NEW adjusters while refreshers bind everyone.
Hand the combined roster to the Learning & Development Specialist as the LMS assignment source.
checklist.done: a single roster covers employed and vendor adjusters and appointed agents, each keyed by adjuster code or agent id and classified NEW or RETURNING.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum against this year's LASH and crop provisions
actions: Map each module to a requirements-matrix row: LASH general and crop-specific loss procedures, appraisal and production worksheets, unit structures, prevented planting and replant provisions, quality adjustment, and the DSSH claim forms from item C01.
Update every module citing a changed handbook section from the C01 diff list, and stamp each module with the reinsurance year and source handbook edition.
Split delivery so classroom sessions total at least 24 hours and total structured hours reach at least 60 for the new-adjuster path.
Publish the curriculum map showing module, hours, delivery mode and the Appendix IV/LASH citation it satisfies.
checklist.done: the published curriculum map reaches 60 structured hours with at least 24 classroom hours and every module carries a current-year citation.

checklist.step: Update and version the competency test bank
actions: Write or refresh test items per LASH loss method the AIP uses — appraisals, production to count, quality adjustment, prevented planting — plus items on sec. 14 claim-form completion and fraud indicators.
Set the pass mark (70% working standard) and the retake rule (one retake after remediation, then re-training) and record both in the procedure.
Retire items invalidated by handbook changes and version the bank as RY<year> so every score traces to the bank version taken.
Load the versioned test into the LMS bound to the new-adjuster path completion.
checklist.done: a versioned competency test aligned to the current LASH is live in the LMS with a documented pass mark and retake rule.

checklist.step: Assign curricula in the LMS with due dates ahead of the season
actions: Load the roster and assign the new-adjuster path to every NEW adjuster and the annual refresher to every RETURNING adjuster and agent.
Set refresher due dates at least 14 days before the earliest sales closing date of the crops each person services (Nov 30 fall crops / Mar 15 spring crops working anchors).
Set new-adjuster due dates relative to hire date with the hard rule that the path plus test must complete before any claim assignment.
Switch on the 30/14/3-day reminder cadence and the manager-escalation copy on overdue items.
checklist.done: every roster member has an LMS assignment with a due date ahead of their earliest sales closing date and reminders armed.

checklist.step: Deliver classroom sessions and capture attendance evidence
actions: Run the classroom sessions to the published module plan, recording session date, topic, instructor and duration in hours.
Collect a signed sign-in sheet (or webinar attendance log with join/leave times for instructor-led virtual sessions) for every session.
Upload the attendance evidence to the LMS session record the same week so classroom hours accumulate on each transcript.
Report any session that ran short of its planned hours to the Learning & Development Specialist so make-up time is scheduled — classroom hours may not be rounded up.
checklist.done: every classroom session has uploaded attendance evidence with actual hours, and transcripts accumulate true classroom time.

checklist.step: Gate claim assignment until accreditation is complete
actions: Configure the claims platform assignment rule to reject any assignment to an adjuster code not flagged accredited for the reinsurance year.
Set the accredited flag only from an LMS feed showing 60 structured hours, 24 classroom hours and a passed competency test — never manually.
Record the accreditation date on the adjuster record so it can be compared to the first-assignment date at test time.

Route any urgent-capacity exception request to the Compliance Manager in writing; pairing an unaccredited trainee with an accredited adjuster for supervised field work is the only permitted workaround, and the accredited adjuster signs the worksheets.
checklist.done: the assignment gate blocks unaccredited adjuster codes, the accredited flag is LMS-fed only, and the sole exception path is supervised pairing with written compliance approval.

checklist.step: Run the annual refresher for returning adjusters and agents
actions: Publish the refresher covering this year's handbook changes, new/changed crop provisions, the C01 form changes and recurring findings from last year's proficiency reviews and complaint root causes (item C05).
Track completion weekly and send the incomplete list to the Claims Director / Manager and the Agency Relations Manager every Monday.
Suspend the accredited flag of any returning adjuster still incomplete at the earliest sales closing date so the assignment gate re-engages.
Record completion rates by week for the April 1 Plan of Operations summary.
checklist.done: refresher completion reaches 100% of active adjusters and agents by the earliest sales closing date or the stragglers' accredited flags are suspended.

checklist.step: Push agent training through the agencies and confirm receipt
actions: Post the agent training bulletin and module links to the agent portal, naming the crops, the sales closing dates and the acreage/production reporting duties covered.
Email each agency principal the assignment list for their agents and require written confirmation of receipt within 5 business days.
Chase non-confirming agencies weekly and report agencies still untrained at 14 days before sales closing to the Compliance Manager.
File the confirmations against the agency record.
checklist.done: every agency principal has confirmed receipt and agent completions are tracked, with untrained agencies escalated 14 days before sales closing.

checklist.step: Verify licensing and appointments line up with training
actions: In NIPR Gateway run the license and appointment status for every appointed crop agent in each state they sell, and run Appointment Renewal where a state's appointment lapses before the sales season.
Check state adjuster-licensing requirements for every state the adjuster roster covers and confirm licenses are current where the state licenses crop adjusters.
Reconcile the NIPR results to the training roster and flag anyone trained but unlicensed, or licensed but never assigned training.
Send the discrepancy list to the Compliance Manager with a clearance deadline ahead of sales closing.
checklist.done: every trained agent and adjuster holds the required current license/appointment, and every discrepancy is cleared or escalated before sales closing.

checklist.step: Run proficiency field reviews on working adjusters
actions: Schedule accompanied field inspections so each active adjuster is observed at least once per reinsurance year, weighting new adjusters and adjusters flagged by complaint or QC findings.
Score each observation against the LASH procedure for the crop — appraisal method, sample counts, worksheet completion, producer communication — on the standard review form.
Record scores in the case tool, set a remediation plan for any failed review, and re-observe within 30 days of remediation training.
Feed recurring weaknesses back to the Instructional Designer for next year's curriculum.
checklist.done: every active adjuster has a scored field review this reinsurance year, failed reviews carry remediation plans with 30-day re-observation, and findings feed the curriculum.

checklist.step: Track completion and chase to 100%
actions: Publish a weekly completion dashboard by population (new adjusters, returning adjusters, agents), showing completed, in-progress, overdue and days to the earliest sales closing date.
Send the overdue list with named managers to the Claims Director / Manager and Agency Relations Manager each Monday.
Escalate any adjuster overdue with an open claim assignment to the Compliance Manager the same day — that combination should be impossible if the gate holds.
Archive the weekly snapshots as the completion trend evidence for the annual test.
checklist.done: a weekly dashboard drives chase-up, gate contradictions are escalated same day, and snapshots are archived as evidence.

checklist.step: Summarize the training program for the April 1 Plan of Operations
actions: Compile the training program description, curriculum map, completion statistics and proficiency review summary required with the Plan of Operations.
Reconcile the reported completion counts to the LMS transcript extract before submission.
Include the package in the Plan of Operations submitted to RMA by April 1 (item C02 step 11 owns the transmission) and store the component with the submission confirmation.
Log any RMA follow-up on the training component and answer it inside the 45-day response discipline.
checklist.done: the training component is reconciled to the LMS, submitted with the April 1 Plan of Operations and any RMA follow-up is tracked to a 45-day due date.

checklist.step: Remediate any claim worked by an unaccredited adjuster
actions: On discovery, pull every claim the adjuster code touched in the reinsurance year from the claims platform and freeze further assignments to that code.

Have the Claims Director / Manager decide per claim: re-inspection by an accredited adjuster, desk re-review of the worksheets, or acceptance with documented rationale — and record the decision on the issue.
Complete the missing training and test before the adjuster returns to the field, and record the accreditation date.
Refer the case to Regulatory Counsel for an RMA disclosure assessment where indemnities were paid on the affected claims.
checklist.done: every affected claim has a recorded re-inspection/re-review decision, the adjuster is retrained before returning, and paid-claim cases are referred to counsel.

checklist.step: Retain the training evidence for the SRA retention period
actions: Archive the requirements matrix, curriculum map, LMS transcripts, sign-in sheets, test scores, proficiency reviews and the Plan of Operations training component under REG-056/C04/RY<year>.
Apply the crop-year-plus-3-years retention label required for records available to FCIC under the SRA.
Confirm retrieval by adjuster code returns the person's full training history — hours, classroom evidence, test score and accreditation date — in one query.
checklist.done: training evidence is archived with a crop-year-plus-3 label and a single adjuster-code query returns the complete accreditation history.

testing.step: Build the population of people who trained and people who worked
actions: Extract every distinct adjuster code appearing on a claim assignment or a transmitted Type 21 claim record in the crop year, with each code's first-assignment date.
Extract the training roster and the LMS completion transcript extract for the same reinsurance year.
Extract the appointed agent list with policies sold in the crop year from the agency/producer management system.
testing.done: three extracts exist — adjuster codes that worked, people who trained, agents who sold — each dated and row-counted.

testing.step: Reconcile workers to the roster and the roster to the transcripts
actions: Match every adjuster code that worked a claim to a roster row; any code with no roster row is an automatic exception — an untracked person adjusted federal crop claims.
Match every roster row to an LMS transcript and list roster members with no transcript.
Reconcile the completion rate claimed in the April 1 Plan of Operations component to the transcript extract and note any variance.
testing.done: every working adjuster code traces to a roster row and a transcript, and the Plan of Operations completion figures reconcile to the LMS.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of NEW adjusters accredited this reinsurance year and 100% of adjusters granted any exception or supervised-pairing arrangement.
Take 20 RETURNING adjusters and 10 agents by seeded random selection across states and vendors.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all new and exception-path adjusters plus a reproducible random selection of returning adjusters and agents.

testing.step: Re-perform the 60/24-hour count from primary evidence
actions: For each sampled NEW adjuster, open the LMS transcript and sum structured hours from the module records — do not accept the transcript total field.
Verify classroom hours against the underlying sign-in sheets or webinar join/leave logs, and count only evidenced hours toward the 24-classroom minimum.
Compare the evidenced totals to the 60-hour and 24-classroom thresholds and list any shortfall.
Treat a module with hours but no attendance evidence as zero classroom hours, not as a documentation gap.
testing.done: each sampled new adjuster has evidenced totals recomputed from primary records against the 60/24 thresholds, with shortfalls listed.

testing.step: Verify the competency test was passed on the current bank before work began
actions: Open each sampled adjuster's test record and confirm the score meets the pass mark, the bank version is the current reinsurance-year version, and retakes followed the documented retake rule.
Confirm the pass date and the accreditation date both pre-date the adjuster's first claim assignment date from the claims extract.
List any adjuster whose first assignment pre-dates the pass date as a breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: every sampled adjuster shows a passed current-version test dated before their first claim assignment, or the breach is listed.

testing.step: Test the assignment gate operation
actions: In the pre-production environment attempt to assign a claim to a test adjuster code with no accredited flag and record the system response.
Inspect the production gate configuration and confirm the accredited flag is populated only by the LMS feed, with no manual-set permission in any active role profile.
Sample the exception log for supervised-pairing arrangements and verify each carries the Compliance Manager's written approval and an accredited co-signer on the worksheets.
Screenshot the rejected assignment and the configuration into the workpaper.
testing.done: the gate rejects unaccredited codes, the flag is LMS-fed only, and every pairing exception carries written approval and a co-signer.

testing.step: Recompute refresher timeliness against sales closing dates
actions: For each sampled RETURNING adjuster and agent, compare the refresher completion date to the earliest sales closing date of the crops/states they service.
Recompute the population-level completion rate as of that date from the archived weekly snapshots and compare it to the 100% threshold.
Confirm the accredited flag was actually suspended for anyone incomplete at the date, using the flag-history log.
testing.done: refresher completion is recomputed against each person's earliest sales closing date and the suspension control is evidenced for stragglers.

testing.step: Verify curriculum content maps to the current Appendix IV and LASH
actions: Re-read Appendix IV and build an independent requirement list before opening the AIP's requirements matrix.
Compare the curriculum map module by module to the independent list and log any requirement with no covering module.
Spot-check two modules for currency: confirm the handbook edition cited is the reinsurance-year edition, not a prior year's.
Log any stale or missing coverage with the exact requirement quoted.
testing.done: an independent Appendix IV requirement list is fully covered by current-year modules, or the gaps are quoted in the workpaper.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with adjuster code or agent id, the specific requirement failed and the claims exposed.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: roster gap, vendor roster not supplied, hours not evidenced, gate bypass, flag set manually, refresher chase failed.
Assign an owner and remediation date, and open re-inspection tasks for claims worked before accreditation.
Refer any pattern of unaccredited adjusting to Regulatory Counsel for an RMA self-disclosure assessment.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and — where claims were exposed — re-inspection tasks and a counsel referral decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold for pre-accreditation claim work and the 100% refresher threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the recomputation and gate-test sections.
Have the independent reviewer, who delivered and scored none of the sampled training, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any self-disclosure recommendation to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C04.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns crop complaint intake, logging, investigation, root-cause remediation and the response to RMA Regional Compliance Office referrals; escalates disputed claim determinations touching mediation, arbitration or National Appeals Division rights to Regulatory Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Section IV(p) and Appendix IV quality control expectations, RMA Manual 14, 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 20 (mediation and arbitration of determinations) and 7 CFR part 11 (USDA National Appeals Division), re-read quarterly and on any Manager's Bulletin touching producer disputes

In-scope processes.value: Complaint intake from producers, agents and the RMA Regional Compliance Office; congressional/USDA inquiries; logging, categorization, investigation against the claim file, written resolution with dispute-rights language; NAD appeal and arbitration tracking; monthly root-cause analysis and remediation of systemic causes across items C01–C04

In-scope systems.value: Complaint cases with category and root-cause codes in the case tool; intake calls logged through the contact center; trends and aging dashboards in Power BI; remediation tasks in the regulatory filing/issue tracker

Compliance procedure documented.value: Crop Complaint Handling Procedure — intake channels, 2-business-day logging and 5-business-day acknowledgement SLAs, category taxonomy, severity triage, investigation steps against the LASH worksheets, dispute-rights language, 45-day RMA response discipline and the root-cause remediation loop

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; refreshed annually and after any change to the sec. 20 arbitration provisions or NAD procedures

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Complaints logged within 2 business days and acknowledged within 5 business days of receipt; RMA/FCIC inquiry and referral responses within 45 days; suspected fraud surfacing in a complaint referred to RMA within 3 business days (item C02 step 9); NAD and arbitration response dates docketed per case

Deadline reminders configured.value: Daily aged-case alert on anything unacknowledged at day 4 or unresolved at day 20; T-10/T-5 alerts on every 45-day RMA response; docket alerts on NAD and arbitration deadlines managed by Regulatory Counsel

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Complaint log with receipt date, channel, category, investigation notes, resolution letter, root-cause code and remediation link, retained crop year plus 3 years for FCIC review

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any complaint substantiating a regulatory breach — late indemnity, misapplied LASH procedure, wrong form edition, unaccredited adjuster — is logged as a compliance exception cross-referenced to the owning item (C01–C04) with remediation and re-check dates

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Compliance Officer signs off closure of every systemic root cause and every complaint whose resolution changed a claim determination or payment

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All complaint cases opened in the period across every intake channel, plus all RMA Regional Compliance Office referrals, congressional inquiries, NAD appeals and sec. 20 arbitration demands, keyed by case id and policy number

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of complaints logged within 2 business days and acknowledged within 5; 100% of RMA responses within 45 days; any substantiated systemic root cause without an opened remediation task is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; monitoring runs weekly, root-cause analysis monthly, and the independent test quarterly over that quarter's complaint population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the complaints and market conduct functions and must not have investigated or resolved any sampled case

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly complaint-monitoring workpaper (population reconciliation, sampled case re-performance, day-count recomputations, remediation traces, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C05

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaint log export with categories, dispositions and day counts, sampled resolution letters and the remediation register, producible to an RMA Regional Compliance Office or USDA OIG request within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns RMA Regional Compliance Office correspondence under the 45-day clock; Regulatory Counsel clears any response conceding a mis-adjusted claim or a determination error before it is sent

checklist.step: Stand up the intake channels and route them to one queue
actions: Configure the contact center complaint line and IVR option so calls tag as CROP-COMPLAINT and land in the single complaints queue.
Add the agent portal complaint form, the policyholder self-service portal form, postal mail scanning and the compliance mailbox as feeding channels into the same queue.
Register the RMA Regional Compliance Office referral mailbox and congressional-inquiry routing from Government Affairs as priority channels with same-day pickup.
Publish the channel list to agents through the Agency Relations Manager so producer complaints are forwarded, not absorbed, by agencies.
checklist.done: every intake channel — phone, portals, mail, RMA referrals, congressional — feeds one queue with priority pickup rules published.

checklist.step: Log every complaint within 2 business days with full identifiers
actions: Open a case within 2 business days of receipt capturing receipt date and channel, complainant name and relationship (insured, agent, third party), policy number, crop, crop year, county and the claim number where the complaint concerns a claim.
Paste or attach the complaint verbatim — letter scan, call recording reference or portal text — so the original wording is preserved.
Link the case to the policy record in the policy administration platform and to the claim file where applicable.
Stamp the source as RMA-REFERRAL where the case arrived from the Regional Compliance Office, because those cases carry the 45-day response clock.
checklist.done: every complaint has a case opened within 2 business days carrying full identifiers, the verbatim complaint and the RMA-referral stamp where applicable.

checklist.step: Acknowledge to the complainant within 5 business days
actions: Send the written acknowledgement naming the case reference, the handler and the expected response window, through the channel the complainant used.
Record the acknowledgement date on the case so the day count is computable at test time.
For RMA referrals, acknowledge to the Regional Compliance Office through the Regulatory Affairs Manager rather than directly.
Never let acknowledgement substitute for investigation — the case stays open until resolved.
checklist.done: every case shows a dated acknowledgement within 5 business days through the correct channel.

checklist.step: Categorize the complaint with the fixed taxonomy
actions: Apply one primary category from the fixed list: claim delay (30-day clock), appraisal/production-count dispute, prevented planting denial, quality adjustment dispute, premium billing/termination, acreage report processing, agent conduct, form/notice content, privacy.
Apply secondary tags for the crop, state, adjuster code and agency involved, because root-cause analysis pivots on these.
Flag any complaint alleging misrepresentation or false production records for the SIU (item C02 step 9's 3-business-day RMA referral clock starts at that discovery).
Re-categorize only with a case note explaining why, so category history survives.
checklist.done: every case carries one primary category, crop/state/adjuster/agency tags and an SIU flag where fraud is alleged.

checklist.step: Triage severity and route to the accountable function
actions: Set severity: HIGH for open 30-day indemnity clocks, terminations in dispute, RMA referrals and congressional inquiries; MEDIUM for determination disputes on closed claims; LOW for service quality.

Route claim determination disputes to the Claims Director / Manager, agent conduct to the Agency Relations Manager and Producer Compliance Manager, billing/termination to the Billing Operations Manager, and SIU flags to the SIU Manager same day.
Set response due dates by severity — HIGH 10 business days, MEDIUM 20, LOW 30 — inside any external clock that binds the case.
Keep case ownership in complaints; the routed function investigates but the Complaints Specialist drives the clock.
checklist.done: every case has a severity, a routed investigating function, a due date inside its external clocks and a named complaints owner.

checklist.step: Investigate against the claim file and the LASH procedure
actions: Pull the claim file: notice of loss, appraisal and production worksheets, adjuster narrative, photos, the executed claim for indemnity and the payment or denial record.

Re-check the disputed step against the LASH procedure for the crop — appraisal method, sample counts, production to count, quality adjustment — and recompute the indemnity where the amount is disputed.
Check the timing facts: signed-claim date, payment date and the 30-day clock; notice generation and delivery dates from the notice log (item C02).
Write a findings note stating whether the complaint is substantiated, partially substantiated or unsubstantiated, with the evidence cited.
Return the findings to the Complaints Specialist within the routed due date.
checklist.done: each investigated case has a findings note grounded in the claim file and LASH recomputation, delivered inside the routed due date.

checklist.step: Resolve in writing with the producer's dispute rights stated
actions: Send the written resolution stating what was found, what is being corrected (payment adjustment, re-inspection, notice re-issue) and the factual basis.

Where the resolution upholds an adverse determination, state the producer's rights: mediation where available, arbitration under 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 20 with its one-year initiation window, and appeal to the USDA National Appeals Division for adverse agency determinations.
Route any resolution changing a claim payment through the Claims Director / Manager for approval before it is sent, and trigger the corrected payment on the claim.
Record the resolution date and attach the letter to the case.
checklist.done: every resolved case has a dated written resolution with corrective action and, where adverse, the sec. 20 and NAD rights stated.

checklist.step: Answer RMA referrals and inquiries inside 45 days
actions: Log every RMA Regional Compliance Office referral or inquiry with its received date and computed 45-day due date in the regulatory record, linked to the complaint case.
Assemble the response from the investigation findings, have Regulatory Counsel clear any admission of a determination error, and send by the due date.
Attach the sent response and transmission confirmation to both the regulatory record and the complaint case.
Request any needed extension in writing before the due date and record RMA's answer.
checklist.done: every RMA item shows a computed 45-day due date and a counsel-cleared response or written extension sent before it.

checklist.step: Docket and manage NAD appeals and arbitration demands
actions: Open a matter for every National Appeals Division appeal and every sec. 20 arbitration demand, docketing the response and hearing dates from the NAD notice or arbitration rules.
Issue a litigation hold on the claim file, adjuster notes and communications for the policy and crop year concerned.
Coordinate the agency record or arbitration submission with the Claims Director / Manager and the Complaints Manager so the complaint case and the legal matter stay linked.
Report outcomes back onto the complaint case, because a reversed determination is a root-cause datapoint.
checklist.done: every appeal and arbitration has a docketed matter, a litigation hold and an outcome recorded back on the complaint case.

checklist.step: Run the monthly root-cause analysis
actions: Publish the monthly view: complaint counts by category, crop, state, adjuster code and agency, with substantiation rates and aging.
Flag any adjuster or agency at more than twice the book-average substantiated-complaint rate and any category trending up two consecutive months.
Drill each flagged cluster to its cases and write the candidate root cause — training gap, form defect, configuration defect, staffing.
Send the analysis to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and the Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: a monthly root-cause analysis is published with flagged clusters, candidate causes and named cases behind each.

checklist.step: Open remediation tasks for systemic causes and route to the owning item
actions: Open one remediation task per substantiated systemic cause, cross-referenced to the owning control: form defects to C01, notice timing to C02, configuration to C03, training to C04.
Name the owner from that item's accountable function and set a remediation date and a re-check method (e.g. complaint rate for the category over the following quarter).
Require adjuster-specific clusters to feed the proficiency review schedule (C04 step 11) and agency clusters to the Agency Relations Manager.
Hold the task open until the re-check shows the cause abated, not merely until the fix shipped.
checklist.done: every systemic cause has a cross-referenced remediation task with owner, date and a re-check that must pass before closure.

checklist.step: Feed complaint outcomes into adjuster QC and training
actions: Receive the monthly list of substantiated claim-handling complaints with adjuster codes and the LASH step that failed.
Schedule the flagged adjusters into accompanied field reviews ahead of unflagged adjusters.
Add recurring failure topics to the annual refresher curriculum via the Instructional Designer.
Confirm back on each complaint case that the QC action was taken, closing the loop.
checklist.done: substantiated claim-handling complaints drive prioritized field reviews and curriculum topics, with the action confirmed on each case.

checklist.step: Report monthly to the Compliance Committee
actions: Present complaint volumes, substantiation rates, aging against the 2/5-day and 45-day clocks, open RMA referrals and the systemic remediation register.
Name any breach of an external clock and its remediation state.
Record the committee's directions in the minutes and carry them as actions on the remediation register.
File the monthly pack in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: a monthly committee pack covers volumes, clocks, RMA referrals and remediations, with directions minuted and actioned.

checklist.step: Reconcile the complaint log to its intake sources quarterly
actions: Pull the quarter's CROP-COMPLAINT tagged calls from the contact center, portal form submissions, scanned mail register and the RMA referral mailbox log.
Match each source record to a case id and list any complaint received but never logged as an automatic exception.
Sample 10 agent-portal messages coded as service requests to check complaints are not being mis-coded out of the population.
File the reconciliation in the quarterly workpaper.
checklist.done: every intake-source record traces to a case id, mis-coding is sampled, and unlogged complaints are raised as exceptions.

checklist.step: Retain complaint records for the SRA retention period
actions: Archive the complaint log, case files, resolution letters, RMA correspondence and root-cause analyses by crop year under REG-056/C05.
Apply the crop-year-plus-3-years retention label required for records available to FCIC, extending holds where a NAD appeal or arbitration remains open.
Confirm retrieval by policy number and by adjuster code returns the linked complaint history.
checklist.done: complaint records are archived with a crop-year-plus-3 label, legal holds extend open disputes, and retrieval works by policy and adjuster code.

testing.step: Build the complaint population for the quarter
actions: Extract every case opened in the quarter with receipt date, channel, category, severity, acknowledgement date, resolution date and root-cause code.
Extract the RMA referral register, the NAD/arbitration matter list and the SIU flag list for the same period.
Row-count each extract and note the counts in the workpaper before any sampling.
testing.done: dated, row-counted extracts exist for cases, RMA referrals, legal matters and SIU flags.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the intake sources independently
actions: Re-pull the quarter's CROP-COMPLAINT tagged calls, portal submissions, mail register and RMA mailbox log without using the complaints team's reconciliation.
Match source records to case ids and list any complaint with no case — each is an automatic exception.
Listen to a sample of 5 complaint-line calls coded as non-complaints to test for suppression at intake.
testing.done: an independent source-to-case reconciliation exists and intake suppression is sampled, with unlogged complaints listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of RMA referrals, congressional inquiries, NAD appeals, arbitration demands and complaints that changed a claim payment.
Take 25 further cases by seeded random selection stratified across categories and severities.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample covers all externally visible and payment-changing cases plus a reproducible stratified random selection.

testing.step: Recompute the logging, acknowledgement and resolution day counts
actions: For each sampled case, read the true receipt date from the source artifact — postmark scan, call timestamp, portal submission time — not the case-entry date.
Recompute business days to case opening and to acknowledgement, and compare to the 2-day and 5-day SLAs.
Recompute days to resolution against the severity due date and list breaches.
Treat a case opened late but backdated as a fail with the discrepancy quoted.
testing.done: every sampled case has recomputed day counts from source timestamps, with late and backdated cases listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the investigation on payment-changing cases
actions: For each case that changed a claim payment, re-open the claim file and independently re-check the disputed LASH step and recompute the corrected indemnity.
Confirm the correction posted to the claim and the corrected payment advice was delivered (item C02 notice log).
Confirm the Claims Director / Manager approval pre-dates the corrected payment.
List any correction that does not reproduce, with the variance.
testing.done: every payment-changing case reproduces on independent recomputation with an approved, delivered correction, or the variance is listed.

testing.step: Verify resolution letters state the required dispute rights
actions: Read each sampled adverse resolution letter and confirm it states mediation availability, arbitration under 7 CFR 457.8 sec. 20 with the one-year initiation window, and the National Appeals Division route for adverse agency determinations.
Confirm the factual basis and the policy provision relied on are stated, not just a conclusion.
Log any letter with missing or paraphrased rights language with the defect quoted.
testing.done: every sampled adverse resolution carries complete sec. 20 and NAD rights language and a stated basis, or the defect is quoted.

testing.step: Recompute the 45-day RMA response clocks
actions: For each RMA referral, read the received date from the referral document itself and recompute the 45-day due date.
Compare to the response sent date on the transmission confirmation and list any breach.
Confirm counsel clearance is evidenced on every response conceding an error.
Confirm any extension was requested and granted in writing before the due date.
testing.done: every RMA referral shows an on-time, counsel-cleared response or a pre-due-date written extension, with breaches listed.

testing.step: Trace systemic root causes to remediation and re-check evidence
actions: List the quarter's substantiated systemic causes from the root-cause analyses and match each to a remediation task with owner and date.
For tasks closed in the period, verify the re-check evidence — the category's complaint rate after the fix — supports closure.
Verify adjuster clusters landed in the C04 field-review schedule and form/config causes landed with the C01/C03 owners.
List any cause with no task, or any task closed without re-check evidence, as exceptions.
testing.done: every systemic cause traces to an owned task and every closure carries re-check evidence, or the gap is listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with case id, policy number, the clock or content requirement failed and the producer impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: intake channel gap, mis-coding, backlog, rights language omitted, RMA clock missed, remediation loop broken.
Assign an owner and remediation date; route any missed RMA clock to the Regulatory Affairs Manager and Regulatory Counsel same day.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment, with RMA-clock misses escalated same day.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the SLA and 45-day compliance rates against the 100% thresholds and the count of substantiated causes without remediation.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — referencing the recomputation and trace sections.
Have the independent reviewer, who investigated no sampled case, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and open RMA-clock breaches to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C05.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with compliance rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Scope the engagement and build the criteria matrix
actions: Open the engagement in AuditBoard under the approved annual plan and define the audited period as the crop year.

Build the criteria matrix: one row per testable rule with its citation — 30-day indemnity payment from the signed claim (7 CFR 457.8 sec. 14), denial letters stating sec. 20 and NAD rights, termination and billing dates from the Special Provisions calendar, April 1 Plan of Operations, weekly transaction cutoff, 3-business-day fraud referral.
Pull the current reinsurance-year date calendar from the C02 owner and attach it as the timing criteria source.
Have the Chief Audit Executive approve the program and criteria before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: an approved engagement exists with a cited criteria matrix and the reinsurance-year date calendar attached as the timing source.

checklist.step: Announce the audit and issue the data request
actions: Send the engagement letter to the Policy Admin Ops Lead, the Claims Director / Manager and the Compliance Manager naming the scope, period and fieldwork dates.
Issue the data request: notice log extract, claims register with signed-claim and payment dates, SIU referral register, transmission batch acceptance reports, and the notice PDF archive access.
Set a 10-business-day return SLA and log receipt of each item against the request.
Chase unreturned items weekly and record delays in the engagement file — data delays are themselves a finding candidate.
checklist.done: the engagement letter is issued and every requested extract is received and logged, or its delay is documented.

checklist.step: Extract the notice population independently
actions: Run the audit's own extract of notices with trigger events in the crop year — policy number, notice type, trigger date, generation date, delivery date, channel, status — rather than relying only on management's notice log.
Extract the underlying trigger events: accepted acreage reports, billing runs, signed claims, denial determinations.
Store both extracts with run dates and row counts in the engagement file.
checklist.done: audit-run extracts of notices and trigger events exist with dated row counts, independent of management's log.

checklist.step: Extract the claims and referral timing data
actions: Extract every claim paid or denied in the crop year with the signed-claim date, determination date, payment issue date and adjuster code.
Extract the SIU case register with discovery dates and RMA referral sent dates.
Extract the weekly transmission batch log with cutoff dates and acceptance reports.
Reconcile claim counts to the claims register control totals before use.
checklist.done: claims, referral and transmission extracts exist and reconcile to control totals.

checklist.step: Reconcile the notice population to trigger events
actions: Match trigger events to notices by type and list every event with no notice — a missing notice is a stronger finding than a late one.
Compare the audit extract to management's notice log and investigate count differences to a cause.
Sign the reconciliation into the workpaper before sampling.
checklist.done: every trigger event maps to a notice or a listed exception, and the audit extract reconciles to management's log with causes for differences.

checklist.step: Build and document the sampling plan
actions: Take 100% of claim denial letters, termination for indebtedness notices, RMA fraud referrals and claims paid beyond day 25 of the 30-day clock.
Take 30 servicing notices (Summary of Coverage, revised Summary, billing) by seeded random selection stratified across crops, states and channels.
Record the seed, strata, population size and selection date in the sampling record so the sample can be re-drawn identically by QA.
checklist.done: a reproducible sampling record covers all high-risk statutory notices plus a stratified random servicing selection.

checklist.step: Test notice content element by element
actions: Open each sampled notice PDF and tick every criteria-matrix content element: denial letters name the policy provision, factual basis and the sec. 20 arbitration and NAD appeal rights; termination notices state amount owed, termination date and reinstatement conditions; Summaries show unit-level liability, share, coverage level and price election.
Compare identifiers on the notice — policy number, crop, county, unit — to the policy record.
Quote every missing or wrong element in the workpaper; do not summarize defects.
checklist.done: each sampled notice has an element-by-element result with defects quoted verbatim.

checklist.step: Recompute every timing clock in the sample
actions: Recompute days from signed-claim date (read from the executed claim form, not the system field) to payment issue for every sampled paid claim against the 30-day standard, and note interest treatment on breaches.
Recompute business days from SIU discovery to RMA referral against the 3-day standard, excluding federal holidays.
Recompute trigger-to-delivery days for servicing notices against their day counts, and verify billing/termination notices landed on the Special Provisions dates for the crop.
Verify the April 1 submission confirmation date and each sampled week's transmission timestamp against the weekly cutoff.
checklist.done: every sampled clock is recomputed from source dates with breaches, interest treatment and cutoff misses scheduled in the workpaper.

checklist.step: Verify proof of delivery and the address of record
actions: For each sampled notice, locate the delivery artifact — mail manifest entry, eDelivery timestamp, or the logged re-attempt for returned mail.
Compare the address on the notice render to the validated address of record at the trigger date.
Flag generation-without-delivery cases separately from late-delivery cases; they are different findings.
File the artifacts against each sampled item in the engagement file.
checklist.done: every sampled notice has a delivery artifact and address match filed, with generation-only cases flagged separately.

checklist.step: Test the upstream controls the notices depend on
actions: Inspect the C01 form-edition control: confirm sampled notices used the edition effective for the crop year, referencing the form inventory register.
Inspect the C03 configuration evidence for the notice triggers: change records, regression results and the production smoke evidence for the audited period.
Where a timing breach clusters on one notice type, trace it to the trigger configuration or the manual queue to identify the control that failed.
Record the control-level conclusion per dependency.
checklist.done: the form-edition and trigger-configuration dependencies are tested and each timing breach is traced to the control that failed.

checklist.step: Clear factual accuracy with management
actions: Send the draft exception schedule to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and Claims Director / Manager for factual review with a 5-business-day window.
Accept corrections only with evidence — a replacement artifact or a corrected date from a source record.
Record each management response verbatim against the exception and hold any unresolved disagreement for the report.
Never drop an exception on assertion alone.
checklist.done: every exception carries management's evidenced response or a recorded disagreement, with none dropped without evidence.

checklist.step: Rate findings and draft the report
actions: Rate each finding on the audit scale: 30-day indemnity breaches, missed RMA referrals and superseded-form acceptance rate High; servicing timeliness below 98% rates Medium; documentation-only defects rate Low.
Write each finding as condition, criteria (with citation), cause, effect and recommendation, quantifying affected policies and dollars where computable.
Cross-reference each finding to the owning control item (C01–C03) so remediation lands with the right owner.
Route the draft through the Chief Audit Executive's review.
checklist.done: a CAE-reviewed draft rates every finding with citation, cause, quantified effect and a cross-referenced owner.

checklist.step: Obtain management action plans with owners and dates
actions: Require a management action plan per finding naming the accountable owner, the corrective action and a completion date; High findings must date inside 90 days.
Reject action plans that restate the recommendation without a mechanism — a plan must name what changes in which system or procedure.
Load the accepted plans into the finding log with automated follow-up dates.
Escalate any refusal to accept a High finding to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: every finding has an accepted action plan with owner, mechanism and date, High findings within 90 days, refusals escalated.

checklist.step: Issue the report ahead of the April 1 submission
actions: Issue the final report to the Audit Committee and the Compliance Committee no later than 30 days after fieldwork close and before the April 1 Plan of Operations is finalized.
Provide the Regulatory Reporting Manager the findings summary relevant to the Plan of Operations quality sections.
Present High findings in person at the next Audit Committee sitting and minute the discussion.
File the issued report in the board portal and the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the report issues within 30 days of fieldwork close, informs the April 1 submission, and High findings are presented and minuted.

checklist.step: Track remediation to validated closure and archive the file
actions: Track each action plan to its date, requesting closure evidence — the changed configuration export, the reissued notice sample, the retrained population — not attestations.
Route validated closures to the Chief Audit Executive for sign-off and report overdue High findings to the Audit Committee quarterly.
Archive the complete engagement file — extracts, sampling record, workpapers, report, action plans — under REG-056/C06/RY<year> with the crop-year-plus-3 retention label.
checklist.done: every action plan closes on evidence with CAE sign-off, overdue Highs are reported quarterly, and the engagement file is archived with retention applied.

testing.step: Pull the engagement file and confirm the audit happened as scoped
actions: Open the engagement file and confirm the approved program, criteria matrix, extracts, sampling record, workpapers and issued report all exist for the reinsurance year.
Compare the audited scope to the C02 notice-type list and record any notice type the audit skipped.
Confirm the report issue date precedes the April 1 Plan of Operations finalization.
testing.done: the engagement file is complete, the scope covers every notice type or the gap is recorded, and issuance pre-dates April 1.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit's population to an independent re-extract
actions: Re-run the notice and claims extracts for the audited crop year using the audit's documented query definitions.
Compare row counts and key totals to the audit's stored extracts and investigate any difference to a cause.
Confirm the audit's reconciliation of trigger events to notices reproduces.
testing.done: an independent re-extract reproduces the audit's population counts and its trigger-to-notice reconciliation.

testing.step: Re-draw the sample from the documented seed
actions: Re-run the seeded selection using the recorded seed, strata and population and compare the drawn items to the audit's sample list.
Confirm the 100% strata (denials, terminations, referrals, day-25-plus claims) are fully present in the tested set.
Any non-reproducing sample or missing stratum item invalidates the affected conclusions and is recorded as a QA exception.
testing.done: the documented seed reproduces the audit's sample and the 100% strata are complete, or the QA exception is recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the content tests on a QA subset
actions: Select 10 audited notices and 5 notices outside the audit sample, and re-test content element by element against the criteria matrix without reading the audit's workpaper first.
Compare results to the audit's conclusions and record any element the audit passed that fails on re-performance.
Treat a defect found in the outside-sample items as evidence the audit's sample missed a defect class, not merely a one-off.
testing.done: a blind re-performance on audited and unaudited items matches the audit's conclusions, or divergences are recorded with their implication.

testing.step: Recompute a subset of the timing schedules
actions: Independently recompute the 30-day indemnity day counts for 10 audited claims from the executed claim forms and payment records.
Independently recompute 5 fraud-referral business-day counts and 5 weekly-cutoff comparisons.
Compare to the audit's schedules cell by cell and record any computational difference.
testing.done: independent recomputation matches the audit's timing schedules, or differences are recorded and resolved to a cause.

testing.step: Verify findings are supported and correctly rated
actions: Read each High and Medium finding against its cited criteria — the SRA section or 7 CFR 457.8 provision — and confirm the criteria actually require what the finding asserts.
Confirm every 30-day breach and superseded-form acceptance found was rated High per the program's rating scale.
Confirm quantifications (affected policies, dollars, interest) trace to workpaper schedules.
Record any finding overstated, understated or resting on a superseded citation.
testing.done: every finding's criteria, rating and quantification withstand legal re-reading, or the defect is recorded.

testing.step: Verify management responses were evidence-based
actions: Sample 5 exceptions cleared during factual-accuracy review and inspect the evidence that removed them.
Confirm no exception was dropped on management assertion alone.
Record any cleared exception whose evidence does not withstand inspection as both a QA exception and a reinstated audit exception.
testing.done: every sampled cleared exception is backed by inspectable evidence, or it is reinstated and recorded.

testing.step: Verify action plans and closures against evidence
actions: Trace every High finding to an accepted action plan with owner and a date inside 90 days.
For closed findings, inspect the closure evidence — configuration export, reissued notices, retrained roster — and confirm the CAE sign-off is dated after the evidence.
List overdue High findings and confirm they were reported to the Audit Committee.
testing.done: every High finding has a compliant plan, closures rest on inspected evidence with dated CAE sign-off, and overdue Highs reached the Audit Committee.

testing.step: Log QA exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per QA exception naming the workpaper, the divergence and the affected audit conclusion.
Assign a root cause: sampling not reproducible, criteria misread, recomputation error, exception cleared without evidence, closure unvalidated.
Assign an owner in the audit function and a remediation date, and require re-issuance of any affected conclusion.
Carry open QA exceptions into the next annual engagement's planning.
testing.done: each QA exception has an issue, coded root cause, audit-function owner, remediation date and any required conclusion re-issuance.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the QA review
actions: State the QA conclusion — the audit can be relied on / relied on with noted exceptions / cannot be relied on — with references to the re-performance sections.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no part of the audited engagement, sign and date the QA memo.
Send the memo to the Chief Audit Executive and the Compliance Committee and file it with the engagement archive under REG-056/C06.
Where the audit cannot be relied on, trigger a re-audit decision at the Audit Committee.
testing.done: a signed QA memo with a stated reliance conclusion is filed with the engagement archive and reported, with re-audit triggered if reliance failed.
