checklist.step: Map SRA oversight obligations to a named board or committee
actions: List every SRA governance obligation as a matrix row: Plan of Operations approval (Section II), training and QC program oversight (Appendix IV — including the 60-hour/24-classroom adjuster standard and competency testing), conflict-of-interest and controlled business limits (Section IV(h)), financial reporting to RMA, complaint and market conduct trends.
Assign each row to the body that owns it — full board, Audit Committee, Compliance Committee — and the frequency it must be considered.
Identify any obligation with no owning body or standing agenda item as a structural gap for the charter review.
Have the General Counsel confirm the mapping in writing.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed matrix assigns every SRA governance obligation to a named body with a review frequency, with structural gaps flagged.

checklist.step: Review and re-adopt the charters annually
actions: Redline each charter against the obligation matrix and last year's charter, adding any missing FCIP standing item and this year's SRA changes.
Confirm each charter states meeting frequency, quorum, membership qualifications and reporting lines.
Present the redlines for committee and board re-adoption and minute the adopting resolutions.
Publish the adopted charters to the board portal with the adoption date, completing the cycle before the April 1 Plan of Operations.
checklist.done: every charter is re-adopted with FCIP standing items before April 1, published with its adoption resolution.

checklist.step: Build the governance calendar for the reinsurance year
actions: Schedule every charter-required meeting for the year and place the FCIP anchors: Plan of Operations approval before April 1, COI certification completion before July 1, the annual Appendix IV training/QC report, and quarterly RMA findings/complaint reviews.

Attach the responsible presenter to each standing item — Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager for training results, Compliance Officer for QC and complaints, Controller for RMA financial reporting.
Arm the 60/30/10-day alerts on each anchor.
Circulate the calendar to all presenters with their material due dates (packs due 7 days before each meeting).
checklist.done: a full-year calendar schedules every required meeting and FCIP anchor with named presenters, pack due dates and armed alerts.

checklist.step: Obtain and minute board approval of the Plan of Operations
actions: Distribute the draft Plan of Operations from the Regulatory Reporting Manager in the board pack at least 7 days before the approval meeting.
Record the resolution approving the Plan and authorizing its submission to RMA, naming the authorized signatory.
Date-check that the approval meeting precedes the April 1 submission and flag any compression to the General Counsel.
Provide the minuted resolution to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the submission record (item C02 step 11).
checklist.done: a minuted board resolution approving the Plan of Operations and its signatory exists and pre-dates the April 1 submission.

checklist.step: Present the annual adjuster training and QC results to the committee
actions: Prepare the annual deck: new-adjuster accreditations with 60-hour/24-classroom completion statistics, competency test pass rates, refresher completion by the sales closing dates, proficiency field review results and remediation cases (from item C04).
Include the QC review results and any claims re-inspected due to unaccredited adjusting.
Present at the committee named in the obligation matrix and answer directed questions on the record.
File the deck and the minute reference in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: the annual training/QC report is presented, minuted and filed, covering accreditation statistics, test results and remediations.

checklist.step: Report RMA findings, complaints and audit results quarterly
actions: Present each quarter: open RMA Regional Compliance Office findings and their 45-day response status, complaint trends and systemic remediations (item C05), and open High findings from the notice audit (item C06).
State any breach of a federal clock — 30-day indemnity, 3-business-day referral, April 1, weekly cutoff — and its cure state.
Minute the committee's directions and register them as tracked actions.
Escalate to the full board any matter counsel assesses as a potential SRA compliance issue affecting reinsurance-year eligibility.
checklist.done: quarterly minutes evidence committee review of RMA findings, complaints and audit results with directions registered as actions.

checklist.step: Collect SRA IV(h) conflict-of-interest certifications before July 1
actions: Build the in-scope roster — directors, officers and employees within SRA IV(h)'s conflict and controlled-business provisions — from the HRIS officer list and the board register.
Issue the annual certification covering prohibited interests in insured entities, controlled business limits and required disclosures, due before the July 1 reinsurance-year start.
Review every disclosed interest, document the determination (permitted, restricted, divestiture required) and the mitigation applied.
Chase non-responders to 100% and report completion to the board with the exceptions register.
checklist.done: 100% of the in-scope roster certifies before July 1, every disclosure carries a documented determination, and completion is reported to the board.

checklist.step: Minute every meeting to the evidentiary standard
actions: Record attendance and quorum, each agenda item considered, the material presented (by pack reference), decisions with resolution numbering and dissents, and follow-up actions with owners.
Circulate draft minutes within 10 business days and present them for adoption at the next meeting.
Index resolutions so any approval — Plan of Operations, charter adoption, remediation direction — is findable by number and date.
Store adopted minutes in the board portal with access controls.
checklist.done: every meeting has adopted, indexed minutes recording quorum, decisions, dissents and owned follow-ups within the 10-day drafting standard.

checklist.step: Track board and committee follow-up actions to closure
actions: Register every minuted action with its owner and due date within 2 business days of minute adoption.
Report open and overdue actions at each subsequent meeting until closed, with the closure evidence referenced.
Escalate actions overdue past 60 days to the committee chair.
Reconcile the action register to the minutes quarterly so no minuted direction goes untracked.
checklist.done: every minuted action is registered, reported until closed with evidence, and the register reconciles to the minutes quarterly.

checklist.step: Maintain the delegation of authority for SRA matters
actions: Maintain the board-adopted delegation naming who may execute the SRA and its amendments, sign the Plan of Operations, and bind the company in RMA correspondence.
Review the delegation at the annual charter cycle and on any officer change.
Confirm every SRA-related execution in the year was made by a delegated signatory, sampling the signature pages.
Re-adopt the delegation by resolution when signatories change.
checklist.done: a current board-adopted delegation covers all SRA executions, verified against sampled signature pages and refreshed on officer changes.

checklist.step: Notify RMA of officer, director and control changes
actions: Receive officer/director change notices from the Corporate Secretary and HRIS feed, and log each with its effective date.
Notify the RMA Regional Office of material changes to the information in the Plan of Operations, tracking the notification under the 45-day response discipline where RMA replies.
For any prospective change of control or material ownership change, obtain FCIC's written approval before closing — route the request through Regulatory Counsel with the transaction timeline.
Record every notification and approval on the regulatory record linked to the board resolution behind it.
checklist.done: every officer/director change is notified to RMA and every change of control shows FCIC written approval obtained before closing.

checklist.step: Orient new directors on FCIP obligations
actions: Deliver the onboarding module covering the SRA structure, the AIP's obligations (training/QC, conflicts, federal clocks), the governance calendar and the director's certification duties, within 60 days of appointment.
Include the current Plan of Operations summary and last year's training/QC report as pre-reading.
Record completion in the LMS and collect the new director's first IV(h) certification at onboarding rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Report onboarding completion to the Corporate Secretary for the governance record.
checklist.done: every new director completes FCIP orientation within 60 days and certifies under IV(h) at onboarding, with completion recorded.

checklist.step: Run the annual board effectiveness review including FCIP oversight
actions: Include in the annual self-assessment questionnaire specific items on FCIP oversight: adequacy of training/QC reporting, visibility of federal clock breaches, and conflict governance.
Compile results and present them with recommended calendar or charter changes.
Feed accepted changes into the next charter review cycle.
File the assessment summary in the governance record.
checklist.done: the annual self-assessment covers FCIP oversight, results are presented, and accepted changes feed the charter cycle.

checklist.step: Reconcile committee activity to the obligation matrix annually
actions: For each obligation matrix row, locate the minute evidence that the owning body considered it at the required frequency this reinsurance year.
List every row with missing or thinner-than-required coverage as a governance gap.
Send the gap list to the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel with proposed calendar fixes for next year.
File the reconciliation as the pre-test self-check.
checklist.done: every obligation row shows minute evidence at the required frequency, or the gap is listed with a proposed fix.

checklist.step: Retain the governance records
actions: Archive charters, calendars, packs, adopted minutes, resolutions, certifications and the action register by reinsurance year under REG-056/C07.
Apply the corporate records retention policy and at least the crop-year-plus-3-years label for FCIC availability.
Confirm retrieval by resolution number and by meeting date returns the minute and its pack together.
checklist.done: governance records are archived with retention applied and retrievable by resolution number and meeting date.

testing.step: Build the governance population for the reinsurance year
actions: Extract from the board portal every meeting held, with body, date, quorum and adopted minutes status, plus the resolution index and the adopted charters.
Extract the COI certification register and the officer/director change list from the HRIS and board register.
Extract the RMA notification log for governance changes from the Internal Regulatory System.
testing.done: dated extracts cover meetings, charters, resolutions, certifications, officer changes and RMA notifications for the year.

testing.step: Reconcile meetings held to charter requirements
actions: Build the meeting-vs-charter matrix: for each body, compare meetings held and quorum achieved to the charter-required frequency.
List every shortfall — missed meeting, inquorate session, minutes never adopted — as an exception.
Confirm each charter in force was re-adopted within the annual cycle.
testing.done: every body's actual meeting cadence and quorum reconcile to its charter, with shortfalls and stale charters listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of meetings carrying an FCIP anchor item — Plan of Operations approval, training/QC report, quarterly RMA/complaint reviews — plus all charters and the full certification register.
Take 5 further meetings by seeded random selection for minute-standard testing.
Record the selection basis and date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample covers every FCIP-anchor meeting, all charters and certifications, plus a documented random minute sample.

testing.step: Verify the training/QC report was genuinely presented and complete
actions: Open the minute and pack for the annual training/QC item and confirm the deck covered new-adjuster 60-hour/24-classroom completion statistics, competency pass rates, refresher completion and proficiency reviews.
Reconcile the deck's completion statistics to the C04 LMS transcript extract for the same reinsurance year.
Confirm the minutes record consideration — questions or directions — not bare receipt.
List any statistic in the deck that does not reconcile to the LMS as an exception.
testing.done: the minuted training/QC presentation is complete and its statistics reconcile to the LMS extract, or variances are listed.

testing.step: Verify the Plan of Operations approval chain
actions: Locate the resolution approving the Plan of Operations and confirm its meeting date precedes the April 1 submission confirmation held in the Internal Regulatory System.
Confirm the signatory on the submitted Plan matches the delegation of authority in force at that date.
Confirm the pack containing the draft Plan was distributed at least 7 days before the meeting.
testing.done: the approval resolution pre-dates the April 1 submission, the signatory matches the delegation, and pack timing met the standard.

testing.step: Re-perform the conflict-of-interest completeness check
actions: Rebuild the in-scope roster independently from the HRIS officer list and the board register as of the certification date.
Match every roster member to a signed certification dated before July 1 and list the gaps.
For sampled disclosed interests, verify a documented determination exists and the mitigation was implemented — e.g. a recusal actually appears in later minutes.
Test one known-interest scenario against SRA IV(h)'s prohibitions to confirm the determination standard is being applied, not just recorded.
testing.done: an independently built roster is fully covered by pre-July 1 certifications and sampled determinations show implemented mitigations.

testing.step: Trace officer and control changes to RMA notifications
actions: Take every officer/director change from the HRIS and board register and match it to an RMA notification on the regulatory record.
For any ownership or control transaction in the year, confirm FCIC written approval is dated before closing — a post-closing approval is an automatic fail.
Confirm each notification links to its underlying board resolution.
testing.done: every governance change traces to an RMA notification and every control change shows pre-closing FCIC approval, or the fail is recorded.

testing.step: Test minute quality and action tracking on the random sample
actions: For each sampled meeting, check the minutes record quorum, decisions with resolution numbers, dissents and owned follow-up actions.
Trace three minuted actions per sampled meeting into the action register and to closure evidence.
Confirm draft minutes circulated within 10 business days and were adopted at the following meeting.
List un-registered actions and unadopted minutes as exceptions.
testing.done: sampled minutes meet the evidentiary standard and their actions trace to registered, evidenced closures, or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the body, period and obligation affected.
Assign a root cause: calendar gap, presenter default, certification chase failed, notification path missed, minute standard lapse.
Assign an owner and remediation date; require a ratification resolution where a required approval was given but not properly minuted, signed off by the General Counsel.
Route any unapproved control change to Regulatory Counsel for immediate FCIC engagement.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner and remediation date, with ratifications counsel-signed and control-change fails escalated immediately.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the results against the thresholds: charter-frequency compliance, annual training/QC presentation, 100% certifications, zero unapproved control changes.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with references to the trace sections.
Sign as the independent reviewer, having drafted none of the sampled minutes or certifications, and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C07.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with threshold results, a stated conclusion and committee reporting exists in the evidence repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the governance disclosure filing calendar for the crop writer — the April 1 Plan of Operations governance exhibits to RMA, the CGAD to the lead state by June 1, the holding-company Form B annual registration, and event-driven FCIC approval requests for changes of control

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 2026 SRA Section II (Plan of Operations content and eligibility) and Section IV(f)(1), the lead state's adoption of the NAIC Corporate Governance Annual Disclosure Model Act (#305) and Model Regulation (#306), and the lead state's Insurance Holding Company System Act (Form A/B/C), re-verified each January before the filing season

In-scope processes.value: Assembling and filing the Plan of Operations governance components (organizational structure, ownership, officers and directors, controls) by April 1; drafting and filing the CGAD by June 1; preparing and filing Form B/C holding-company registration; monitoring for event triggers — control changes, officer changes, material affiliate agreements — and making the FCIC and lead-state filings they require

In-scope systems.value: The filing calendar, submission records and confirmations live in the Internal Regulatory System; board approvals in the board portal; statutory data feeding Form B exhibits reconciles to the annual statement filed via the NAIC statutory reporting platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Governance Disclosure Filing Procedure — filing inventory with legal citations, component owners and internal due dates, review and approval chain (drafter → General Counsel → board where required), submission channels (RMA Regional Office mailbox, lead-state portal, NAIC filing where applicable) and confirmation capture

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel; re-approved each January after the filing inventory is re-verified against current statutes and the new SRA

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Plan of Operations to RMA by April 1; CGAD to the lead-state commissioner by June 1; Form B by the lead state's annual due date; Form A and FCIC prior approval before any change of control closes; material changes to filed information reported to RMA and answered within the 45-day response discipline

Deadline reminders configured.value: Internal Regulatory System alerts at T-60/T-30/T-10 for April 1, June 1 and the Form B date, plus an event-trigger checklist embedded in the corporate development deal workflow so control-change filings start at term-sheet stage

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed documents, submission confirmations, board approval resolutions and regulator correspondence retained 7 years per the corporate records policy and at least crop year plus 3 years for FCIC availability

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any late, incomplete or omitted governance filing — and any control change progressed without its FCIC/Form A approvals — is logged with the filing, days late, cause and the cure filing date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off the cure of every filing exception and personally owns regulator engagement on any approval obtained late

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every governance filing due in the calendar year — Plan of Operations governance components, CGAD, Form B/C — plus every officer/control/affiliate-agreement event in the year and the filings each event required

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of calendar filings submitted by their statutory dates with confirmations held; zero control changes closed without prior FCIC approval and lead-state Form A approval; any required filing discovered missing is an automatic fail regardless of age

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligations are annual (April 1, June 1, Form B date) plus event-driven; the independent test runs annually after June 1, with an event-trigger check each quarter

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted, approved or filed any tested submission

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual governance-filings workpaper (independent filing-inventory rebuild, submission traces, event-to-filing traces, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-056/C08

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The filing register with confirmations, filed CGAD and Form B copies and board approvals, producible to RMA or the lead-state department within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager owns RMA correspondence; the Statutory Reporting Manager and Regulatory Filing Specialist own lead-state holding-company correspondence; General Counsel clears every response touching ownership or control

checklist.step: Rebuild the governance filing inventory each January
actions: List every governance filing with its citation and due date: Plan of Operations to RMA by April 1 (2026 SRA Section II), CGAD to the lead state by June 1 (Model #305 as adopted), Form B by the lead state's annual date, plus event-driven Form A and FCIC control-change approvals.
Re-read the lead state's current statutes and bulletins for changed due dates, formats or confidentiality procedures and update the rows.
Load the inventory into the filing calendar with T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts and named owners per row.
Have the General Counsel approve the inventory as the year's authoritative filing list.
checklist.done: a counsel-approved filing inventory with citations, due dates, owners and armed alerts is loaded for the year.

checklist.step: Confirm the lead state and its filing mechanics
actions: Confirm the lead state of the insurance holding company system with the General Counsel and record the basis (domicile of the top-tier insurer, lead-state designation).
Verify the CGAD filing channel the lead state accepts — secure portal, dedicated mailbox — and its confidentiality submission procedure, and record both on the inventory row.
Verify the Form B channel and any state-specific exhibits beyond the NAIC model set.
Record the state contact for filing questions and the date each channel was verified.
checklist.done: the lead state, each filing's channel and confidentiality procedure are verified and recorded with a dated basis.

checklist.step: Assign component owners and internal due dates
actions: Break each filing into components with owners: organizational and ownership structure (Corporate Secretary), officers/directors and biographical data (Board Governance Lead), financials and dividends (Controller), affiliate agreements (General Counsel), governance framework narrative (Board Governance Lead).
Set internal due dates at least 20 business days before each statutory date to leave review and approval room.
Open a tracked task per component and review progress at a standing weekly check during the filing season.
Escalate any component trending late to the General Counsel at T-30.
checklist.done: every filing component has an owner and an internal due date 20 business days ahead of the statutory date, tracked weekly.

checklist.step: Assemble the Plan of Operations governance exhibits
actions: Compile the Section II exhibits: legal entity and ownership chart, officers and directors with changes since last year, the organizational structure for FCIP delivery, and the control and QC program descriptions (drawing the training component from item C04 step 13).
Obtain the financial exhibits from the Controller reconciled to the statutory annual statement.

Run the year-over-year diff and confirm every change in ownership, officers or structure was already notified to RMA (item C07 step 11) — an unnotified change surfacing in the Plan is itself an exception to log.
Deliver the assembled governance exhibits for board approval and the April 1 submission.
checklist.done: the governance exhibits are assembled, reconciled to the statutory statement, diffed year-over-year and cleared of unnotified changes.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval and submit the Plan by April 1
actions: Confirm the board resolution approving the Plan of Operations is minuted (item C07 step 4) and the signatory matches the delegation of authority.
Submit the Plan to the RMA Regional Office by April 1 through the designated channel and capture the submission confirmation.
Log the submission and confirmation on the filing register the same day.
Track any RMA revision request under the 45-day response discipline on the same record.
checklist.done: the board-approved Plan is submitted by April 1 with a captured confirmation and any revision requests tracked to 45-day due dates.

checklist.step: Draft the CGAD
actions: Draft to the Model #305/#306 content requirements: the governance framework and structure, board and committee composition and selection, director qualifications and independence, policies on ethics and conflicts (referencing the SRA IV(h) certification program), performance evaluation, compensation oversight and management succession.
Update from last year's CGAD, describing material changes in the year — new committees, charter amendments, officer changes — rather than restating boilerplate.
Reconcile every factual statement to the adopted charters and minutes in the board portal.
Route the draft to the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel review chain by the internal due date.
checklist.done: a current-year CGAD draft meets the Model #305 content list, describes the year's material changes and reconciles to charters and minutes.

checklist.step: Clear the CGAD confidentiality and legal review
actions: Review the draft for accuracy and privilege, and mark the filing with the confidentiality assertions the lead state's CGAD statute provides for.
Confirm the CGAD signatory (CEO or Corporate Secretary as the state prescribes) and prepare the signature page.
Record the review notes and the cleared version in the legal document system.
Release the cleared version to the Regulatory Filing Specialist for submission.
checklist.done: a counsel-cleared CGAD with confidentiality assertions and the prescribed signatory is released for filing.

checklist.step: File the CGAD with the lead state by June 1
actions: Submit the signed CGAD through the lead state's verified channel before June 1, following the state's confidentiality submission procedure.
Capture the submission confirmation or portal receipt and log it on the filing register the same day.
Diarize any state acknowledgement or deficiency letter and route questions to the Board Governance Lead with the response deadline.
Confirm no other state requires a copy this year (a non-lead state may request one on 30 days' notice) and log any such request when received.
checklist.done: the CGAD is filed before June 1 with a logged confirmation, and any state follow-up or copy request is diarized with a deadline.

checklist.step: Prepare the Form B holding-company registration statement
actions: Prepare the Form B exhibits: the holding-company organizational chart with ownership percentages, biographical affidavits for new directors/officers, affiliate agreements and amendments, shareholder dividends paid, and the financial statements of the ultimate controlling person.
Reconcile the org chart and affiliate transactions to Schedule Y of the statutory annual statement so the two filings cannot diverge.
Attach Form C (summary of changes) highlighting what changed from the prior year's registration.
Route the package through General Counsel review by the internal due date.
checklist.done: the Form B/C package is complete, reconciled to Schedule Y and counsel-reviewed by the internal due date.

checklist.step: File Form B by the lead state's due date
actions: Submit the Form B/C package through the lead state's holding-company filing channel by the state's annual due date.
Capture the filing confirmation and log it on the filing register the same day.
Diarize the state's review and route any deficiency or follow-up to the Statutory Reporting Manager with a response deadline.
Record any state-imposed conditions on the register for next year's preparation.
checklist.done: Form B/C is filed by the state due date with a logged confirmation and any deficiencies tracked to deadlines.

checklist.step: Monitor for event triggers and start filings at deal stage
actions: Maintain the event-trigger checklist in the corporate development workflow: any acquisition or disposition of control, new material affiliate agreement, extraordinary dividend, or officer/director change trips a filing assessment.

For a prospective change of control, open the filing workstream at term-sheet stage: FCIC prior written approval (routed via Regulatory Counsel and the Regulatory Affairs Manager) and the lead-state Form A, both to be approved before closing.
For material affiliate agreements and extraordinary dividends, prepare the Form D prior-notice filing within the state's notice period before the transaction takes effect.
Log every trigger event and its filing determination — filed, or documented as not required with the reason — on the register.
checklist.done: every trigger event has a logged filing determination, and control-change approvals are obtained before closing, not after.

checklist.step: Answer regulator follow-ups inside their windows
actions: Log every RMA or lead-state follow-up on a governance filing with its received date and computed due date — 45 days for RMA items, the stated deadline for state deficiency letters.
Assign the drafting owner (component owner from the original filing) and set an internal draft date at the halfway point.
Route every response touching ownership or control through General Counsel before sending.
Attach the sent response and confirmation to the original filing record.
checklist.done: every follow-up carries a computed due date and an owner, and responses are counsel-cleared and confirmed on the filing record.

checklist.step: Maintain the filing register as the single record
actions: Keep one register row per filing and per event determination: filing name, citation, due date, submitted date, channel, confirmation reference, approvals behind it, follow-ups and their status.
Reconcile the register quarterly against the inventory and against the board resolution index (a resolution approving a transaction implies a filing determination must exist).
Flag any register row missing a confirmation reference for immediate chase.
Publish the register status in the quarterly Compliance Committee pack.
checklist.done: the register carries a confirmed row for every filing and event, reconciles quarterly to the inventory and resolutions, and is reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Brief the board on filing status annually
actions: Present the annual filing summary after June 1: each filing, its submission date versus the statutory date, open follow-ups and any exceptions cured in the year.
Highlight next year's date changes discovered in the January inventory rebuild.
Minute the presentation and any board directions.
File the summary with the governance records.
checklist.done: an annual filing summary is presented and minuted after June 1 covering dates met, open follow-ups and cured exceptions.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence
actions: Archive filed documents, confirmations, board approvals and regulator correspondence by filing and year under REG-056/C08.
Apply the 7-year corporate records retention and at least the crop-year-plus-3 label for FCIC availability.
Confirm retrieval by filing name and year returns the filed document and its confirmation together.
checklist.done: filing evidence is archived with retention applied and retrievable as filed-document-plus-confirmation pairs.

testing.step: Rebuild the filing obligation list independently
actions: Re-derive the year's required governance filings from source law without using the team's inventory: SRA Section II (April 1 Plan of Operations), the lead state's CGAD statute (June 1), the holding-company act (Form B date, Form A, Form D).
Compare the independent list to the filing register and record any obligation the register lacks — a missing obligation is a stronger finding than a late filing.
Confirm the lead-state determination basis is documented and still correct.
testing.done: an independently derived obligation list is fully covered by the register, or missing obligations are recorded.

testing.step: Build the event population from independent sources
actions: Extract the year's officer/director changes from the HRIS and board register, dividends and affiliate agreements from board resolutions and the legal contract repository, and any control transactions from corporate development records.
Match each event to a register row with a filing determination.
List every event with no determination as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every governance event found in independent sources maps to a filing determination, or the gap is listed.

testing.step: Test every calendar filing against its statutory date
actions: For the Plan of Operations, CGAD and Form B/C, read the submission confirmation and compare the submitted date to April 1, June 1 and the state's Form B date respectively — the population is small, so test 100%.
Verify each confirmation reference actually opens to a stored confirmation artifact, not just a register entry.
List any filing submitted late, or any confirmation that cannot be produced, as a fail.
testing.done: all three annual filings show stored confirmations dated on or before their statutory dates, or fails are listed.

testing.step: Re-read the CGAD against the model content requirements
actions: Read the filed CGAD against the lead state's enacted #305/#306 content list item by item — governance framework, board composition and qualifications, policies, evaluation, compensation oversight, succession.
Verify the described structures against the adopted charters and the C07 minutes; a described committee that never met per its charter is a finding here and in C07.
Confirm the confidentiality assertion followed the state's procedure and the prescribed signatory signed.
Quote any content gap or factual mismatch.
testing.done: the filed CGAD covers the enacted content list and matches the governance records, or gaps are quoted.

testing.step: Reconcile Form B to Schedule Y and the resolutions
actions: Compare the Form B organizational chart and ownership percentages to Schedule Y of the filed statutory annual statement and list any divergence.
Trace sampled affiliate agreements and dividends disclosed on Form B/C to their authorizing board resolutions and, where required, to Form D prior-notice filings.
Confirm biographical affidavits exist for every director/officer added in the year.
testing.done: Form B reconciles to Schedule Y, sampled transactions trace to resolutions and prior notices, and new-officer affidavits are complete.

testing.step: Verify approval chains pre-date submissions
actions: Confirm the board resolution approving the Plan of Operations pre-dates the April 1 submission and the signatory matched the delegation in force.
Confirm General Counsel review is evidenced on the CGAD and Form B before their filing dates.
List any submission that went out before its required approval as a fail.
testing.done: every tested submission shows its approval chain completed before filing, or the sequence break is listed as a fail.

testing.step: Trace control changes to pre-closing approvals
actions: For each control transaction in the event population, locate the FCIC written approval and the lead-state Form A approval and compare both dates to the closing date.
Read the deal file to confirm the filing workstream opened at term-sheet stage as the procedure requires.
Treat any approval dated after closing as an automatic fail escalated to the General Counsel the same day.
Where no control transaction occurred, evidence the nil population from the corporate development records.
testing.done: every control change shows FCIC and Form A approvals dated before closing, or the fail is escalated same day; a nil population is evidenced.

testing.step: Recompute follow-up response clocks
actions: For each regulator follow-up in the year, recompute the due date from the received date — 45 days for RMA, the stated deadline for state letters — and compare to the response sent date.
Confirm counsel clearance is evidenced on every response touching ownership or control.
List breaches and unanswered items.
testing.done: every follow-up shows an on-time, appropriately cleared response, or breaches are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the filing or event, days late and the regulator affected.
Assign a root cause: inventory gap, component owner default, approval sequencing, trigger checklist missed, confirmation not captured.
Assign an owner and remediation date; require the missing or corrective filing to be made and its confirmation attached before closure.
Route any unapproved control change or missed statutory filing to the General Counsel for regulator engagement and a self-report assessment.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, coded root cause, owner, remediation date and an attached cure filing, with statutory misses routed to counsel.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the results against the thresholds: 100% on-time calendar filings with confirmations, zero unapproved control changes, zero missing obligations.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — referencing the independent rebuild and trace sections.
Sign as the independent reviewer, having drafted and filed none of the tested submissions, and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Compliance Committee and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper under REG-056/C08.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with threshold results, a stated conclusion and committee reporting exists in the evidence repository.
